title.zh: 卷三百四十五 列傳第一百〇四 劉安世 鄒浩 田晝 王回 曾誕 陳瓘 任伯雨
title.en: Volume 345 Biographies 104: Liu Anshi, Zou Hao, Tian Zhou, Wang Hui, Ceng Dan, Chen Guan, Ren Boyu
title.raw: 卷三百四十五 列傳第一百〇四 劉安世 鄒浩 田晝 王回 曾誕 陳瓘 任伯雨 Volume 345 Biographies 104: Liu Anshi, Zou Hao, Tian Zhou, Wang Hui, Ceng Dan, Chen Guan, Ren Boyu

sentences.zh: 劉安世

translations.literal: Liu Anshi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anshi

sentences.zh: 劉安世，字器之，魏人。

translations.literal: Liu Anshi, style name Qizhi, was a man of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anshi, whose style name was Qizhi, came from Wei.

sentences.zh: 父航，第進士，歷知虞城、犀浦縣。

translations.literal: His father Hang passed the jinshi examination and successively served as magistrate of Yucheng and Xipu counties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Hang earned the jinshi degree and in turn governed Yucheng and Xipu counties.

sentences.zh: 虞城多姦猾，喜寇盜；

translations.literal: Yucheng had many crafty scoundrels who delighted in banditry and theft.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng teemed with cunning rascals prone to robbery.

sentences.zh: 犀浦民弱而馴。

translations.literal: The people of Xipu were weak and docile.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xipu were meek and tractable.

sentences.zh: 航為政，寬猛急緩不同，兩縣皆治。

translations.literal: In governing, Hang applied leniency and severity, urgency and ease differently, yet both counties were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Hang tailored his rule to each county—now lenient, now severe—but both ended up well governed.

sentences.zh: 知宿州，押伴夏使，使者多所要請，執禮不遜，且欲服毬文金帶入見，航皆折正之。

translations.literal: As prefect of Suzhou he escorted Xia envoys; the envoys made many demands, were insolent in ceremony, and wished to wear ball-pattern gold belts when received in audience—Hang corrected all of this.
translations.idiomatic: While prefect of Suzhou he escorted Western Xia envoys who pressed many demands, showed discourtesy in protocol, and even wanted to enter audience wearing ornamental gold belts—Hang put a stop to every abuse.

sentences.zh: 以群牧判官為河南監牧使。

translations.literal: From the post of herd-management judge he became Henan supervisory commissioner for herds.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from herd-management judge to Henan supervisory commissioner for herds.

sentences.zh: 持節冊夏主秉常，凡例所遺寶帶、名馬，卻弗受。

translations.literal: Bearing credentials to invest Xia ruler Bingchang, he declined all customary gifts of precious belts and famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned to invest the Xia ruler Bingchang, he refused every customary gift of jeweled belts and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 還，上《禦戎書》，大略云：「辨士好為可喜之說，武夫徼冀不貲之寵，或為所誤，不可不戒。

translations.literal: On his return he submitted a "Book on Guarding the Frontier," stating in summary: "Persuaders love to offer pleasing talk; warriors hope for extravagant favor—one may be misled by them and must be on guard."
translations.idiomatic: After returning he submitted a memorial on frontier defense, warning in essence that smooth talkers and ambitious generals who crave extravagant rewards can mislead policy and must be heeded with caution.

sentences.zh: 」為河北西路轉運使。

translations.literal: " He served as transport commissioner for Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed transport commissioner for Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 熙寧大旱求言，航論新政不便者五，又上書言：「人主不可輕失天下心，宜乘時有所改為，則人心悅而天意得矣。

translations.literal: During the great drought of the Xining era, when the throne sought counsel, Hang set forth five points on the inconveniences of the new policies and further memorialized: "The sovereign must not lightly lose the hearts of the realm; he should seize the moment to make reforms, and popular hearts will be pleased and Heaven's intent obtained."
translations.idiomatic: When a severe drought in the Xining era prompted the court to solicit advice, Hang listed five flaws in the new policies and urged that a ruler must not lightly forfeit the people's trust—timely reforms would win both popular favor and Heaven's approval.

sentences.zh: 」不報，乃請提舉崇福宮，起知涇、相二州。

translations.literal: " Receiving no response, he requested appointment as superintendent of Chongfu Palace, then was recalled to govern Jing and Xiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went unanswered; he then sought a post superintending Chongfu Palace and was later recalled to govern Jing and Xiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 王師西征，徙知陝府。

translations.literal: When the imperial army marched west, he was transferred to govern Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial forces marched west, he was transferred to govern Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時倉卒軍興，餽餉切急，縣令佐至荷校督民，民多棄田廬，或至自盡。

translations.literal: At the time the army was raised in haste; supplies were urgently needed; county magistrates and assistants went so far as to shackle and drive the people, many abandoning fields and homes, some even taking their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: The war mobilization was sudden and supply demands crushing; magistrates shackled commoners to force deliveries until many fled their farms and some killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 航獨期會如平日，事更以辦。

translations.literal: Hang alone kept deadlines as on ordinary days, and affairs were handled all the more efficiently.
translations.idiomatic: Hang alone kept to ordinary schedules, and affairs were handled all the more efficiently.

sentences.zh: 終太僕卿。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Minister of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Minister of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 安世少時持論已有識。

translations.literal: Even in youth Anshi's opinions already showed discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man Anshi's views already showed unusual discernment.

sentences.zh: 航使監牧時，文彥博在樞府，有所聞，每呼安世告之，安世從容言：「王介甫求去，外議謂公且代其任。

translations.literal: When Hang served as herd commissioner, Wen Yanbo was in the Bureau of Military Affairs; hearing things, he would summon Anshi and tell him. Anshi said calmly: "Wang Jiefu seeks to leave office; outside opinion holds that you will soon take his post."
translations.idiomatic: While Hang was herd commissioner, Wen Yanbo at the Bureau of Military Affairs would hear rumors and call Anshi in to share them. Anshi replied calmly, "Wang Anshi is seeking to resign, and rumor has it you will replace him."

sentences.zh: 」彥博曰：「安石壞天下至此，後之人何可為？

translations.literal: " Yanbo said: "Anshi has ruined the realm to this point—what can later men do?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yanbo said, "Anshi has brought the realm to ruin—what can anyone do afterward?"

sentences.zh: 」安世拱手曰：「安世雖晚進，竊以為未然。

translations.literal: " Anshi bowed with hands joined and said: "Though I am a latecomer, I venture to think otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi bowed and said, "I am only a junior man, but I do not believe it is hopeless."

sentences.zh: 今日新政，果順人所欲而為人利乎？

translations.literal: Do today's new policies truly accord with what people desire and bring them benefit?
translations.idiomatic: Do the new policies truly follow the people's wishes and serve their interests?

sentences.zh: 若不然，公當去所害，興所利，反掌間耳。

translations.literal: If not, you should remove what harms and promote what benefits—it is but the turn of a hand.
translations.idiomatic: If not, you need only remove what harms and raise what helps—a matter of a moment's decision.

sentences.zh: 」彥博默不應，他日見航，歎獎其堅正。

translations.literal: " Yanbo was silent and did not reply; another day, meeting Hang, he praised Anshi's firm integrity.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanbo said nothing; later, meeting Hang, he praised Anshi's steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，不就選。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination but did not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination but declined to take up office.

sentences.zh: 從學於司馬光，諮盡心行己之要，光教之以誠，且令自不妄語始。

translations.literal: He studied under Sima Guang, inquiring into the essentials of devoting one's heart and conducting oneself; Guang taught him sincerity and told him to begin by not speaking falsely.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Sima Guang, who taught him the discipline of wholehearted integrity, beginning with the rule never to speak falsely.

sentences.zh: 調洺州司法參軍，司戶以貪聞，轉運使吳守禮將按之，問於安世，安世云：「無之。

translations.literal: Assigned as judicial aide in Ming Prefecture, the revenue registrar was known for greed; transport commissioner Wu Shouli was about to investigate and asked Anshi, who said: "There is none."
translations.idiomatic: Posted as judicial aide in Ming Prefecture, he learned the revenue registrar was notoriously corrupt; when transport commissioner Wu Shouli was about to investigate and asked Anshi, Anshi answered, "There is nothing to it."

sentences.zh: 」守禮為止。

translations.literal: " Shouli stopped the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouli dropped the case.

sentences.zh: 然安世心常不自安，曰：「司戶實貪而吾不以誠對，吾其違司馬公教乎！

translations.literal: Yet Anshi's heart was never at ease, saying: "The registrar is truly greedy, yet I did not answer with sincerity—have I violated Master Sima's teaching?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Anshi could not rest easy, saying, "The registrar was truly corrupt, yet I was not truthful—have I betrayed Master Sima's teaching?"

sentences.zh: 」後讀揚雄《法言》「君子避礙則通諸理」，意乃釋。

translations.literal: " Later, reading in Yang Xiong's Fayan that "the gentleman, avoiding obstruction, thereby penetrates all principles," his mind was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he read in Yang Xiong's Fayan that "when the gentleman sidesteps obstruction, he grasps every principle," and his mind was eased.

sentences.zh: 光入相，薦為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: When Guang entered the chancellorship, he recommended Anshi as corrector in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang became chief councilor, he recommended Anshi as Secretariat corrector.

sentences.zh: 光薨，宣仁太后問可為臺諫於呂公著，公著以安世對。

translations.literal: When Guang died, Empress Dowager Xuanren asked Lü Gongzhu who could serve on the remonstrance bureaus; Gongzhu named Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: After Guang's death, Empress Dowager Xuanren asked Lü Gongzhu who might serve as a remonstrance official; he named Anshi.

sentences.zh: 擢右正言。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 時執政頗與親戚官，安世言：「祖宗以來，大臣子弟不敢受內外華要之職。

translations.literal: At the time those in power often gave offices to relatives. Anshi said: "Since the founding ancestors, sons and younger brothers of great ministers dared not accept splendid posts inside and outside the court."
translations.idiomatic: The ruling faction was handing out offices to kin. Anshi said, "Since the founding of the dynasty, ministers' sons and brothers did not dare take the most glittering posts at court or in the provinces."

sentences.zh: 自王安石秉政，務快私意，累聖之制，掃地不存。

translations.literal: Since Wang Anshi held power, bent on gratifying private wishes, the institutions of successive sage emperors were swept away without trace.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Anshi took power, pursuing private advantage, institutions built by successive emperors were swept away.

sentences.zh: 今廟堂之上，猶習故態。

translations.literal: Now above in the temple hall, the old ways are still practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at court today the old habits persist.

sentences.zh: 」因歷疏文彥博以下七人，皆耆德魁舊，不少假借。

translations.literal: " He then successively impeached Wen Yanbo and six others below him—all elders of virtue and eminent veterans—showing them no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: " He then impeached in turn Wen Yanbo and six other senior statesmen, sparing none of the court's most venerable figures.

sentences.zh: 章惇以強市昆山民田罰金，安世言：「惇與蔡確、黃履、邢恕素相交結，自謂社稷之臣，貪天之功，僥幸異日，天下之人指為『四凶』。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun was fined for forcibly buying commoners' fields in Kunshan. Anshi said: "Dun, Cai Que, Huang Lü, and Xing Shu have long been allied, calling themselves pillars of the state, usurping Heaven's merit, hoping for future fortune—the people of the realm call them the 'Four Evils.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun was fined for forcibly buying farmland in Kunshan, Anshi said, "Dun, Cai Que, Huang Lü, and Xing Shu have long been a clique, styling themselves pillars of the state and stealing credit from Heaven—the realm calls them the Four Evils."

sentences.zh: 今惇父尚在，而別籍異財，絕滅義理，止從薄罰， 何以示懲？

translations.literal: Now Dun's father is still alive, yet he has set up a separate household register and divided property, utterly violating moral principle—yet he receives only a light penalty. How can this serve as a warning?
translations.idiomatic: Dun's father is still alive, yet he has registered a separate household and divided the family estate in violation of filial duty—yet he receives only a light fine. How will that deter others?

sentences.zh: 」會吳處厚解釋確《安州詩》以進，安世謂其指斥乘輿，犯大不敬，與梁燾等極論之，竄之新州。

translations.literal: " When Wu Chuhou submitted an exegesis of Que's "Anzhou Poems," Anshi held that it reviled the imperial carriage and constituted grave disrespect; with Liang Tao and others he argued forcefully, and Que was banished to Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wu Chuhou submitted an interpretation of Que's Anzhou poems implicating the throne, Anshi argued with Liang Tao and others that it was lese-majeste; Que was banished to Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰相范純仁至於御史十人，皆緣是去。

translations.literal: Chief councilor Fan Chunren down to ten censors—all left office on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilor Fan Chunren and ten censorial officials all lost their posts because of it.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人兼左司諫，進左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist of Attendance and concurrently Left Bureau Remonstrator, then advanced to Left Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was made diarist of attendance and Left Bureau remonstrator, then promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 有旨暫罷講筵，民間驩傳宮中求乳婢，安世上疏諫曰：「陛下富於春秋，未納后而親女色。

translations.literal: An edict temporarily suspended the lecture sessions; among the people it was joyfully rumored that the palace was seeking wet nurses. Anshi memorialized in remonstrance: "Your Majesty is in the prime of youth, has not yet taken an empress, yet is intimate with women's charms."
translations.idiomatic: When lectures were suspended, rumor spread that the palace was seeking wet nurses. Anshi memorialized, "Your Majesty is young, has not yet taken an empress, yet is already drawn to women's charms."

sentences.zh: 願太皇太后保祐聖躬，為宗廟社稷大計，清閑之燕，頻御經帷，仍引近臣與論前古治亂之要，以益聖學，無溺於所愛而忘其可戒。

translations.literal: May the Grand Empress Dowager protect the sacred person for the great design of the ancestral temples and altars of state; in leisurely repose, frequently attend the classics curtain, and still bring in close ministers to discuss the essentials of order and disorder in antiquity, to enrich the sage learning—do not drown in what you love and forget what must be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: May the Grand Empress Dowager guard your health for the sake of the dynasty; in your leisure, attend the lecture hall often, summon close ministers to discuss how past ages rose and fell, enrich your learning, and do not let affection blind you to what you must guard against.

sentences.zh: 」哲宗俛首不語，后曰：「無此事，卿誤聽爾。

translations.literal: " Emperor Zhezong bowed his head and said nothing; the empress dowager said: "There is no such matter—you have heard wrongly."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Zhezong bowed his head in silence; the empress dowager said, "There is no such thing—you have been misinformed."

sentences.zh: 」明日，后留呂大防告之故。

translations.literal: " The next day the empress dowager detained Lü Dafang and told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day she kept Lü Dafang behind and explained what had happened.

sentences.zh: 大防退，召給事中范祖禹使達旨。

translations.literal: Dafang withdrew; she summoned Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu to convey her intent.
translations.idiomatic: After Dafang left, she summoned Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu to relay her message.

sentences.zh: 祖禹固嘗以諫，於是兩人合辭申言之甚切。

translations.literal: Zuyu had already remonstrated on this; now the two men joined their words and stated it with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu had already remonstrated on the matter; the two men now spoke together with renewed urgency.

sentences.zh: 鄧溫伯為翰林承旨，安世言其「出入王、呂黨中，始終反覆。

translations.literal: Deng Wenbo served as Hanlin Academician Recipient; Anshi said of him: "He moved in and out of the Wang and Lü factions, reversing himself from start to finish."
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Wenbo became Hanlin Academician Recipient, Anshi said he had "shuttled between the Wang and Lü factions, reversing himself at every turn."

sentences.zh: 今之進用，實係君子小人消長之機。

translations.literal: His present advancement truly concerns the waxing and waning of gentlemen and petty men.
translations.idiomatic: His promotion now truly marks whether gentlemen or petty men are gaining the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 乞行免黜。

translations.literal: I beg that he be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 」不報，遂請外，改中書舍人，辭不就。

translations.literal: " Receiving no response, he then requested an outside post, was changed to Secretariat Drafter, and declined to take office.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went unanswered; he sought a provincial post, was named Secretariat drafter, and declined.

sentences.zh: 以集賢殿修撰提舉崇福宮，才六月，召為寶文閣待制、樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: As Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Talents he was made superintendent of Chongfu Palace; after only six months he was summoned as Awaiting Draft at the Baowen Pavilion and Chief Receiver at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Compiler in the Hall of Assembled Talents he superintended Chongfu Palace; after only six months he was recalled as Baowen Pavilion awaiting draft and chief receiver at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 范純仁復相，呂大防白后欲令安世少避，后曰：「今既不居言職，自無所嫌。

translations.literal: When Fan Chunren again became chief councilor, Lü Dafang informed the empress dowager that he wished Anshi to keep somewhat apart; she said: "Now that he no longer holds a remonstrance post, there is naturally nothing to suspect."
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Chunren returned as chief councilor, Lü Dafang asked the empress dowager to have Anshi keep his distance; she replied, "He no longer holds a remonstrance post, so there is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」又語韓忠彥曰：「如此正人，宜且留朝廷。

translations.literal: " She also told Han Zhongyan: "Such an upright man ought for the time being to be kept at court."
translations.idiomatic: " She also told Han Zhongyan, "A man this upright ought to remain at court for now."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " The plan was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿復光祿卿，分司，安世爭以為不可，不聽。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing was restored as Director of the Imperial Sacrifices with a nominal commission; Anshi argued strenuously that this should not be done, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Huiqing was restored as Director of the Imperial Sacrifices on a nominal commission, Anshi protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 出知成德軍。

translations.literal: He was sent out to govern Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 章惇用事，尤忌惡之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun held power, he especially hated Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Dun took power, he especially hated Anshi.

sentences.zh: 初黜知南安軍，再貶少府少監，三貶新州別駕，安置英州。

translations.literal: At first he was demoted to govern Nan'an Army; again demoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshops; a third time demoted to Assistant Administrator of Xin Prefecture and settled in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was first demoted to Nan'an Army, then to Vice Director of the Palace Workshops, then to assistant administrator of Xin Prefecture and exiled to Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 同文館獄起，蔡京乞誅滅安世等家，讒雖不行，猶徙梅州。

translations.literal: When the Tongwen Hall case arose, Cai Jing begged to exterminate the families of Anshi and others; though the slander did not succeed, Anshi was still transferred to Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tongwen Hall case broke, Cai Jing sought to wipe out Anshi's family; though that plot failed, Anshi was still transferred to Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 惇與蔡卞將必置之死，因使者入海島誅陳衍，諷使者過安世，脅使自裁。

translations.literal: Dun and Cai Bian were determined to put him to death; using the envoy who went to the sea isle to execute Chen Yan, they hinted that the envoy pass by Anshi and coerce him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Dun and Cai Bian were determined to kill him; they sent the envoy who executed Chen Yan on a distant island to pass by Anshi and pressure him to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 又擢一土豪為轉運判官，使殺之。

translations.literal: They also promoted a local strongman to transport vice-commissioner to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: They also promoted a local strongman to transport vice-commissioner with orders to murder him.

sentences.zh: 判官疾馳將至梅，梅守遣客來勸安世自為計。

translations.literal: The vice-commissioner galloped in haste and was about to reach Mei; the prefect of Mei sent a guest to urge Anshi to make plans for himself.
translations.idiomatic: The vice-commissioner raced toward Mei; the prefect sent a visitor urging Anshi to save himself.

sentences.zh: 安世色不動，對客飲酒談笑，徐書數紙付其僕曰：「我即死，依此行之。

translations.literal: Anshi's expression did not change; facing the guest he drank wine and talked and laughed, slowly writing several sheets and handing them to his servant, saying: "When I am about to die, act according to this."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's face never changed; he drank and chatted with the visitor, then slowly wrote several pages for his servant, saying, "When I die, follow these instructions."

sentences.zh: 」顧客曰：「死不難矣。

translations.literal: " Turning to the guest he said: "Death is not difficult."
translations.idiomatic: " He told the visitor, "Death is not difficult."

sentences.zh: 」客密從僕所視，皆經紀同貶當死者之家事甚悉。

translations.literal: " The guest secretly looked at what the servant held—all were detailed arrangements for the household affairs of fellow exiles who were likewise marked for death.
translations.idiomatic: " The visitor peeked at the papers: they were detailed instructions for the families of fellow exiles also marked for death.

sentences.zh: 判官未至二十里，嘔血而斃，危得免。

translations.literal: Before the vice-commissioner had gone twenty li, he vomited blood and died; Anshi narrowly escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li short of Mei the vice-commissioner vomited blood and died; Anshi narrowly escaped.

sentences.zh: 安世儀狀魁碩，音吐如鐘。

translations.literal: Anshi's bearing was imposing and tall; his voice rang like a bell.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was tall and imposing; his voice rang like a bell.

sentences.zh: 初除諫官，未拜命，入白母曰：「朝廷不以安世不肖，使在言路。

translations.literal: When first appointed remonstrance official, before accepting the commission he went in and told his mother: "The court, not deeming Anshi unworthy, has placed me on the path of remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: When first appointed remonstrance official, before accepting the commission he told his mother, "The court has placed me on the remonstrance path despite my unworthiness."

sentences.zh: 倘居其官，須明目張膽，以身任責，脫有觸忤，禍譴立至。

translations.literal: If I hold this office, I must speak with open eyes and bold heart, taking responsibility upon my own person; should I give offense, disaster and punishment will come at once.
translations.idiomatic: If I take the post I must speak boldly and bear the consequences myself; one offense and punishment will come at once.

sentences.zh: 主上方以孝治天下，若以老母辭，當可免。

translations.literal: The sovereign is just now governing the realm through filial piety; if I plead my aged mother, I should be able to decline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor governs through filial piety; if I plead my aged mother, I may be excused.

sentences.zh: 」母曰：「不然，吾聞諫官為天子諍臣，汝父平生欲為之而弗得，汝幸居此地，當捐身以報國恩。

translations.literal: " His mother said: "Not so. I have heard that remonstrance officials are the sovereign's disputing ministers. Your father all his life wished to be one but could not. You are fortunate to hold this post—you should give your body to repay the state's grace."
translations.idiomatic: " His mother said, "No. Remonstrance officials are the emperor's disputing ministers. Your father wanted that post all his life and never obtained it. You are fortunate to hold it—give your life to repay the state's grace."

sentences.zh: 正得罪流放，無問遠近，吾當從汝所之。

translations.literal: Even if you rightly incur offense and are exiled, no matter how far, I shall follow wherever you go.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you are punished and exiled, no matter how far, I will follow you.

sentences.zh: 」於是受命。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: " He then accepted the commission.

sentences.zh: 在職累歲，正色立朝，扶持公道。

translations.literal: In office for many years, he stood at court with stern countenance, upholding public justice.
translations.idiomatic: For years in office he stood at court with stern countenance, upholding public justice.

sentences.zh: 其面折廷爭，或帝盛怒，則執簡卻立，伺怒稍解，復前抗辭。

translations.literal: When he confronted others in open debate at court, if the emperor was greatly angered, he would hold his memorial tablet, step back, and stand aside, waiting until the anger eased slightly, then advance again to speak in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: When he debated face to face at court and the emperor flew into rage, he would step back with his memorial tablet, wait until the anger cooled, then advance and argue again.

sentences.zh: 旁侍者遠觀，蓄縮悚汗，目之曰「殿上虎」，一時無不敬懾。

translations.literal: Attendants watching from afar shrank back in dread and broke into a cold sweat, calling him the "Tiger of the Hall"—for a time none failed to respect and fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants watching from afar shrank back in dread and called him the Tiger of the Hall—none failed to respect and fear him.

sentences.zh: 家居未嘗有惰容，久坐身不傾倚，作字不草書，不好聲色貨利。

translations.literal: At home he never showed a lazy expression; seated long, his body did not lean; in writing he did not use cursive script; he did not delight in sound, color, goods, or profit.
translations.idiomatic: At home he never looked idle; he sat for hours without slouching, wrote only in regular script, and cared nothing for pleasure, wealth, or gain.

sentences.zh: 其忠孝正直，皆則象司馬光。

translations.literal: His loyalty, filial piety, and uprightness all took Sima Guang as their model.
translations.idiomatic: In loyalty, filial piety, and integrity he modeled himself on Sima Guang.

sentences.zh: 年既老，群賢凋喪略盡，巋然獨存，而名望益重。

translations.literal: When he had grown old, the host of worthies had largely passed away; he alone stood towering, and his renown grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: In old age, as most of his generation of worthies had died, he alone remained standing, and his renown only grew.

sentences.zh: 梁師成用事，能生死人，心服其賢，求得小吏吳默嘗趨走前後者，使持書來，啖以即大用，默因勸為子孫計，安世笑謝曰：「吾若為子孫計，不至是矣。

translations.literal: Liang Shicheng held power and could decide men's life and death; admiring Anshi's worth, he found the minor clerk Wu Mo, who had once attended him, and had him bring a letter, tempting him with imminent great employment. Mo therefore urged him to plan for his descendants. Anshi smiled and declined: "If I planned for descendants, I would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shicheng, who held life-and-death power at court, admired Anshi and sent a former attendant, clerk Wu Mo, with a letter promising imminent high office. Mo urged him to think of his descendants. Anshi smiled and declined, "If I had planned for my descendants, I would not be here."

sentences.zh: 吾欲為元祐全人，見司馬光於地下。

translations.literal: I wish to be a whole man of the Yuanyou era and meet Sima Guang in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to remain a whole man of the Yuanyou era and meet Sima Guang in the grave.

sentences.zh: 」還其書不答。

translations.literal: " He returned the letter without reply.
translations.idiomatic: " He returned the letter unanswered.

sentences.zh: 死葬祥符縣。

translations.literal: He died and was buried in Xiangfu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in Xiangfu County.

sentences.zh: 後二年，金人發其塚，貌如生，相驚語曰：「異人也！

translations.literal: Two years later the Jurchens opened his tomb; his appearance was as in life, and they said to one another in alarm: "An extraordinary man!"
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Jurchen soldiers opened his tomb; his body looked alive, and they exclaimed in alarm, "An extraordinary man!"

sentences.zh: 」為之蓋棺乃去。

translations.literal: " They closed the coffin for him and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: " They closed the coffin and left.

sentences.zh: 鄒浩，字志完，常州晉陵人。

translations.literal: Zou Hao, style name Zhiwan, was a man of Jinling in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Hao, whose style name was Zhiwan, came from Jinling in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調揚州、潁昌府教授。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as instructor in Yang and Yingchang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was posted as instructor in Yang and Yingchang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 呂公著、范純仁為守，皆禮遇之。

translations.literal: When Lü Gongzhu and Fan Chunren served as prefects, both treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Gongzhu and Fan Chunren served as prefects, both treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 純仁屬撰樂語，浩辭。

translations.literal: Chunren asked him to compose celebratory verses; Hao declined.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren asked him to compose celebratory verses; Hao declined.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「翰林學士亦為之。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Hanlin academicians also do this."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Hanlin academicians do this as well."

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「翰林學士則可，祭酒、司業則不可。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "For Hanlin academicians it is permissible; for the Chancellor of the Directorate and Vice Chancellor it is not."
translations.idiomatic: " Hao replied, "That may be so for Hanlin academicians, but not for a Chancellor of the Directorate or Vice Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 」純仁敬謝。

translations.literal: " Chunren respectfully apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " Chunren apologized respectfully.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，上疏論事，其略曰：「人材不振，無以成天下之務。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he memorialized on affairs of state, stating in summary: "Talents are not flourishing, and there is no means to accomplish the tasks of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era he memorialized on state affairs, arguing in essence that talent is not flourishing and the realm's business cannot be accomplished.

sentences.zh: 陛下視今日人材，果有餘邪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, regarding today's talents, are there truly enough?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, do you believe today's talent pool is truly sufficient?

sentences.zh: 果不足邪？

translations.literal: Or truly not enough?
translations.idiomatic: Or truly insufficient?

sentences.zh: 以為不足，則中外之百執事未嘗不備。

translations.literal: If you hold them insufficient, then the hundred offices inside and outside the court have never been unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: If you say they are insufficient, every post at court and in the provinces is nonetheless filled.

sentences.zh: 以為有餘，則自任以天下之重者幾人？

translations.literal: If you hold them sufficient, then how many take upon themselves the heavy burden of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If you say they are sufficient, how many truly shoulder the weight of the realm?

sentences.zh: 正色昌言不承望風旨者幾人？

translations.literal: How many speak with stern countenance and forthright words, not bending to prevailing winds and hints?
translations.idiomatic: How many speak with stern countenance and forthright words, refusing to trim their sails to the prevailing wind?

sentences.zh: 持刺舉之權以肅清所部者幾人？

translations.literal: How many hold the power of impeachment and investigation to purge and discipline their jurisdictions?
translations.idiomatic: How many have wielded the power of recommendation and impeachment to purge and discipline their jurisdictions?

sentences.zh: 承流宣化而使民安田里者幾人？

translations.literal: How many carry forward edicts and transform the people so the people dwell peacefully in their fields?
translations.idiomatic: How many have carried forward imperial policy and spread its benefits so that the people could live in peace on their farms?

sentences.zh: 民貧所當富也，則曰水旱如之何；

translations.literal: When the people are poor and ought to be enriched, they say, "What can be done about flood and drought?"
translations.idiomatic: When the people are poor and ought to be made prosperous, they say, "What can we do about floods and droughts?"

sentences.zh: 官冗所當澄也，則曰民情不可擾；

translations.literal: When the bureaucracy is redundant and ought to be thinned, they say the people's affairs must not be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When the bureaucracy is bloated and ought to be thinned, they say the people's affairs must not be disturbed.

sentences.zh: 人物所當求也，則曰從古不乏材；

translations.literal: When talent ought to be sought, they say there has never been a shortage of capable men since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When worthy talent ought to be recruited, they say there has never been a shortage of capable men since ancient times.

sentences.zh: 風俗所當厚也，則曰不切於時變，是皆不明義理之過也。」

translations.literal: "When customs ought to be strengthened, they say it is not suited to changing times—all these are faults of failing to understand right principle."
translations.idiomatic: When customs ought to be strengthened, they say such efforts are out of step with the times—all these errors arise from failing to understand right principle."

sentences.zh: 蘇頌用為太常博士，來之邵論罷之。

translations.literal: Su Song had him appointed Doctor of the Grand Commandant's Office; Lai Zhishao argued for his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Su Song had him appointed Doctor of the Grand Commandant's Office, but Lai Zhishao argued successfully for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 後累歲，哲宗親擢為右正言。

translations.literal: Several years later, Emperor Zhezong personally promoted him to Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, Emperor Zhezong personally promoted him to Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 有請以王安石《三經義》發題試舉人者，浩論其不可而止。

translations.literal: When someone proposed using Wang Anshi's Explanations of the Three Classics as examination topics, Hao argued against it and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When someone proposed using Wang Anshi's Explanations of the Three Classics as examination topics for the civil service exams, Hao argued against it and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 陝西奏邊功，中外皆賀，浩言：「先帝之志而陛下成之，善矣。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi reported frontier victories and all congratulated, Hao said: "The late emperor's intent and Your Majesty's fulfillment are excellent.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi reported military victories on the frontier, congratulations poured in from across the court, but Hao said, "Your Majesty has fulfilled the late emperor's ambition—a fine achievement indeed.

sentences.zh: 然兵家之事，未戰則以決勝為難，既勝則以持勝為難，惟其時而已。

translations.literal: Yet in military affairs, before battle deciding victory is hard; after victory holding victory is hard—it depends on timing alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in military affairs, the hardest thing before battle is to win, and after victory the hardest thing is to hold the victory—it all comes down to timing.

sentences.zh: 苟為不然，將棄前功而招後患。

translations.literal: If not so, former achievements will be abandoned and later troubles invited.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, you will squander past gains and invite future disaster.

sentences.zh: 願申敕將帥，毋狃屢勝，圖惟厥終。」

translations.literal: I beg that orders be sent to commanders not to grow complacent after repeated victories, but to plan to the end."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that orders be reinforced to the commanders not to grow complacent after repeated victories, but to think through to the final outcome."

sentences.zh: 京東大水，浩言：「頻年水異繼作，雖盈虛之數所不可逃，而消復之方尤宜致謹。

translations.literal: When eastern regions suffered great floods, Hao said: "Strange floods have struck in succession year after year; though cycles of fortune and disaster cannot be escaped, methods of relief especially require care.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern regions were hit by severe flooding, Hao said, "Strange floods have struck year after year. Though the cycles of fortune and disaster cannot be escaped, we must be all the more diligent in finding ways to alleviate suffering and restore order.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『惟先格王正厥事。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: 'Only when the former king corrected his conduct
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, 'It was only when the former king corrected his own conduct

sentences.zh: 』不以為數之當然，此消復之實也。」

translations.literal: ' and did not treat calamity as merely the natural course of fate—this is the true way to relieve disaster and restore order.'"
translations.idiomatic: that he did not treat calamity as merely the natural course of fate—this is the true way to relieve disaster and restore order.'"

sentences.zh: 蹇序辰看詳元祐章奏，公肆詆欺，輕重不平。

translations.literal: When Jian Xuchen reviewed Yuanyou memorials, he openly slandered and deceived, applying punishments unevenly.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian Xuchen reviewed Yuanyou-era memorials, he openly slandered and deceived, applying punishments unevenly.

sentences.zh: 浩言：「初旨但分兩等，謂『語及先帝』並『語言過差』而已；

translations.literal: Hao said: "The original intent divided only two grades—'remarks concerning the late emperor' and 'remarks overstepping bounds' alone;
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "The original intent was only to distinguish two categories—remarks concerning the late emperor and remarks that overstepped proper bounds—

sentences.zh: 而今所施行，混然莫辨。

translations.literal: but what is now enforced is confused and indistinguishable.
translations.idiomatic: but what is now being enforced is a confused mess that no one can tell apart.

sentences.zh: 以其近似難分之跡，而典刑輕重隨以上下，是乃陛下之威福操柄下移於近臣。

translations.literal: Because of traces hard to distinguish as similar, punishments rise and fall accordingly—this shifts Your Majesty's power of reward and punishment to close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Because of ambiguities that are hard to distinguish, punishments are applied with arbitrary severity—and thus Your Majesty's power to reward and punish has been ceded to favorites at court.

sentences.zh: 願加省察，以為來事之監。」

translations.literal: I beg added reflection, taking this as a warning for future affairs."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to reflect carefully on this, and use it as a warning for the future."

sentences.zh: 章惇獨相用事，威虐震赫，浩所言每觸惇忌，仍上章露劾，數其不忠侵上之罪，未報。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun alone held power as chief minister, his cruelty terrifying; Hao's words each provoked Dun's resentment, yet he still submitted open impeachments listing crimes of disloyalty and encroachment on the sovereign—no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun dominated the government as sole chief minister, his cruelty and violence terrifying the court. Hao's every remark provoked Dun's resentment, yet Hao still submitted open impeachments listing Dun's crimes of disloyalty and encroachment on imperial authority—but received no response.

sentences.zh: 而賢妃劉氏立，浩言：

translations.literal: When Noble Consort Liu was enthroned, Hao said:
translations.idiomatic: When Noble Consort Liu was made empress, Hao said:

sentences.zh: 「立后以配天子，安得不審。

translations.literal: "To install an empress as consort to the Son of Heaven—how can one not proceed with utmost care?
translations.idiomatic: "To install an empress as consort to the Son of Heaven—how could one not proceed with the utmost care?

sentences.zh: 今為天下擇母，而所立乃賢妃，一時公議，莫不疑惑，誠以國家自有仁祖故事，不可不遵用之爾。

translations.literal: You are choosing a mother for the realm, yet the one enthroned is a Noble Consort; public opinion at the time was all doubtful—truly the state has precedents from Emperor Renzong that must be observed.
translations.idiomatic: You are choosing a mother for the empire, yet the woman enthroned is a Noble Consort. Public opinion at the time was unanimous in its alarm—and rightly so, for the dynasty has precedents from Emperor Renzong that must be observed.

sentences.zh: 蓋郭后與尚美人爭寵，仁祖既廢后，並斥美人，所以示公也。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo and Lady Shang competed for favor, Emperor Renzong deposed the empress and also expelled the Beautiful Lady—to show impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo and Lady Shang competed for favor, Emperor Renzong deposed the empress and also expelled the Beautiful Lady—to demonstrate impartiality.

sentences.zh: 及立后，則不選於妃嬪而卜於貴族，所以遠嫌，所以為天下萬世法也。

translations.literal: When he took a new empress, he did not choose from consorts but divined among noble families—to remove suspicion and set a law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: When he took a new empress, he did not choose from among his consorts but selected from the noble families—to remove suspicion and to set a precedent for all ages.

sentences.zh: 陛下之廢孟氏，與郭后無以異。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's deposition of Lady Meng was no different from Empress Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's deposition of Lady Meng was no different from the case of Empress Guo.

sentences.zh: 果與賢妃爭寵而致罪乎？

translations.literal: Was she truly deposed for competing with the Noble Consort for favor?
translations.idiomatic: Was she truly deposed because she competed with the Noble Consort for favor?

sentences.zh: 抑其不然也？

translations.literal: Or was it not so?
translations.idiomatic: Or was that not the reason at all?

sentences.zh: 二者必居一於此矣。

translations.literal: One of these two must be true.
translations.idiomatic: One of these two explanations must be true.

sentences.zh: 孟氏罪廢之初，天下孰不疑立賢妃為后。

translations.literal: When Lady Meng was first deposed, who in the realm did not suspect the Noble Consort would be made empress?
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Meng was first deposed, who in the empire did not assume the Noble Consort would be made empress?

sentences.zh: 及讀詔書，有『別選賢族』之語，又聞陛下臨朝慨歎，以為國家不幸，至於宗景立妾，怒而罪之，於是天下始釋然不疑。

translations.literal: But when the edict was read with language to "select from another noble house," and when Your Majesty was heard sighing at court that the state had met misfortune—and even punished Zong Jing for taking a concubine—then the realm was reassured.
translations.idiomatic: But when the edict was read and its language promised to "select from another noble house," and when Your Majesty was heard sighing at court that the country had met with misfortune—and even punished Zong Jing for taking a concubine—then the empire was reassured and ceased to suspect.

sentences.zh: 今竟立之，豈不上累聖德？

translations.literal: Now that she has actually been enthroned, does this not weigh upon sacred virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Now that she has actually been enthroned, does this not tarnish Your Majesty's sacred virtue?

sentences.zh: 臣觀白麻所言，不過稱其有子，及引永平、祥符事以為證。

translations.literal: Looking at the white hemp edict, it says nothing beyond praise that she had borne a son and cites Yongping and Xiangfu precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at the enthronement edict, I find nothing in it beyond praise that she had borne a son, and references to the precedents of the Yongping and Xiangfu reigns.

sentences.zh: 臣請論其所以然，若曰有子可以為后，則永平貴人未嘗有子也，所以立者，以德冠後宮故也。

translations.literal: Let me discuss the reasoning: if having a son qualifies one to be empress, the Noble Lady of Yongping had no son; she was made empress because her virtue surpassed the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Let me examine the reasoning. If having a son qualifies one to be empress, then the Noble Lady of the Yongping era had no son; she was made empress because her virtue surpassed all others in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 祥符德妃亦未嘗有子，所以立者，以鍾英甲族故也。

translations.literal: The Virtuous Consort of Xiangfu likewise had no son; she was made empress because she came from a distinguished noble house.
translations.idiomatic: The Virtuous Consort of the Xiangfu era likewise had no son; she was made empress because she came from a distinguished noble house.

sentences.zh: 又況貴人實馬援之女，德妃無廢后之嫌，迥與今日事體不同。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Noble Lady was in fact Ma Yuan's daughter, and the Virtuous Consort bore no taint of a deposed empress—these cases differ utterly from today's matter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Noble Lady was in fact the daughter of Ma Yuan, and the Virtuous Consort bore no taint of a deposed empress—these cases are utterly unlike today's situation.

sentences.zh: 頃年冬，妃從享景靈宮，是日雷變甚異。

translations.literal: Only a few winters ago, when the consort attended sacrifice at Jingling Palace, thunder struck that day—a portent of the strangest kind.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few winters ago, when the consort attended a sacrifice at Jingling Palace, thunder struck that day—a portent of the strangest kind.

sentences.zh: 今宣制之後，霖雨飛雹，自奏告天地宗廟以來，陰淫不止。

translations.literal: Since the enthronement decree, torrential rains and hail have fallen without cease since sacrifices were reported to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Since the enthronement decree was proclaimed, torrential rains and hail have fallen without cease from the day sacrifices were reported to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 上天之意，豈不昭然！

translations.literal: Can Heaven's intent be any clearer?
translations.idiomatic: Can Heaven's warning be any clearer?

sentences.zh: 考之人事既如彼，求之天意又如此，望不以一時改命為難，而以萬世公議為可畏，追停冊禮，如初詔行之。」

translations.literal: Human affairs point one way and Heaven's signs another; I beg Your Majesty not to cling to a decision already made but to heed the judgment of posterity—halt the enthronement and abide by the original edict."
translations.idiomatic: Human affairs point one way and Heaven's signs point another. I beg Your Majesty not to cling to a decision already made, but to heed the judgment of posterity—halt the enthronement ceremony and abide by the original edict."

sentences.zh: 帝謂：「此亦祖宗故事，豈獨朕邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This too follows ancestral precedent—is it only I who have done so?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "This too follows ancestral precedent—is it only I who have done so?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「祖宗大德可法者多矣，陛下不之取，而效其小疵，臣恐後世之責人無已者紛紛也。

translations.literal: Hao replied: "The ancestors offered many great virtues worth emulating, yet Your Majesty ignores those and copies their minor flaws—I fear posterity will never stop finding fault."
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "The ancestors offered many great virtues worth emulating, yet Your Majesty ignores those and copies their minor flaws. I fear posterity will never stop finding fault."

sentences.zh: 」帝變色，猶不怒，持其章躊躇四顧，凝然若有所思，付外。

translations.literal: The emperor flushed but did not rage; he held the memorial, hesitated and looked about, lost in thought, then referred it outward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed but did not lose his temper. He held the memorial, hesitated and looked about, lost in thought, then referred it outward for action.

sentences.zh: 明日，章惇詆其狂妄，乃削官，羈管新州。

translations.literal: The next day Zhang Dun denounced him as arrogant; Hao was stripped of office and exiled under restraint to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhang Dun denounced him as arrogant and reckless. Hao was stripped of his office and exiled under restraint to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡卞、安惇、左膚繼請治其祖送者王回等，語在他傳。

translations.literal: Cai Bian, An Dun, and Zuo Fu then petitioned for punishment of those who had escorted him, including Wang Hui—the account appears in other biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Bian, An Dun, and Zuo Fu then petitioned for punishment of those who had escorted him into exile, including Wang Hui—the full account appears in other biographies.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，亟召還，復為右正言，遷左司諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, Hao was quickly recalled, restored as Right Rectifier, and promoted to Left Remonstrating Official.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, Hao was quickly recalled, restored as Right Rectifier, and promoted to Left Remonstrating Official.

sentences.zh: 上疏謂：「孟子曰：『左右諸大夫皆曰賢，未可也；

translations.literal: In a memorial he quoted Mencius: "When all ministers at Your side say a man is worthy, that is not enough;
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he quoted Mencius: "When all the ministers at Your Majesty's side say a man is worthy, that is not enough;

sentences.zh: 國人皆曰賢，然後察之，見賢焉，然後用之。

translations.literal: only when all the people of the realm say he is worthy should you investigate—and only when you find him worthy should you appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: only when all the people of the realm say he is worthy should you investigate—and only when you find him worthy should you appoint him.

sentences.zh: 左右諸大夫皆曰不可，勿聽；

translations.literal: When all ministers at Your side say a man must go, do not listen;
translations.idiomatic: When all the ministers at Your side say a man must go, do not listen;

sentences.zh: 國人皆曰不可，然後察之，見不可焉，然後去之。

translations.literal: only when all the people of the realm say he must go should you investigate—and only when you find him unfit should you remove him.
translations.idiomatic: only when all the people of the realm say he must go should you investigate—and only when you find him unfit should you remove him.

sentences.zh: 』於是知公議不可不恤，獨斷不可不謹。

translations.literal: From this we know public opinion must be heeded and independent judgment exercised with caution.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that public opinion must be heeded and that independent judgment must be exercised with caution.

sentences.zh: 蓋左右非不親也，然不能無交結之私；

translations.literal: Those at Your side are indeed intimate, yet they cannot be free of private alliances;
translations.idiomatic: Those at Your side are indeed intimate counselors, yet they cannot be free of private alliances;

sentences.zh: 諸大夫非不貴也，然不能無恩仇之異。

translations.literal: and the grandees are indeed eminent, yet they cannot be free of personal grudges.
translations.idiomatic: and the grandees are indeed eminent men, yet they cannot be free of personal grudges and debts of favor.

sentences.zh: 至於國人皆曰賢，皆曰不可，則所謂公議也。

translations.literal: But when all the people of the realm speak with one voice—that is public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: But when all the people of the realm speak with one voice—that is public opinion.

sentences.zh: 公議之所在，概已察之，必待見賢然後用，見不 可然後去，則所謂獨斷也。

translations.literal: To heed public opinion is to investigate broadly; to wait until you see merit before appointing and unfitness before removing—that is independent judgment.
translations.idiomatic: To heed public opinion is to investigate broadly; to wait until you see merit before appointing and see unfitness before removing—that is independent judgment.

sentences.zh: 惟恤公議於獨斷未形之前，謹獨斷於公議已聞之後，則人君所以致治者，又安有不善乎？

translations.literal: If you heed public opinion before deciding on your own, and exercise judgment only after public opinion is heard, how could governance fail to be good?
translations.idiomatic: If you heed public opinion before deciding on your own, and exercise independent judgment only after public opinion has been heard, how could your governance fail to be good?

sentences.zh: 伏見朝廷之事，頗異於即位之初，相去半年，遽 如是，自今以往，將如之何？

translations.literal: I observe court affairs have already diverged from accession—after only half a year, so sudden a change! What will the future hold?
translations.idiomatic: I observe that affairs at court have already diverged sharply from how they stood at Your Majesty's accession—after only half a year, so sudden a change! What will the future hold?

sentences.zh: 願陛下深思之。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to reflect deeply on this."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to reflect deeply on this."

sentences.zh: 改起居舍人，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diary Attendant and promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Diary Attendant and then promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下善繼神宗之志，善述神宗之事，孝德至矣。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "Your Majesty has admirably continued Shenzong's ambitions and commemorated his achievements—filial piety could scarcely be greater.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Your Majesty has admirably continued Emperor Shenzong's ambitions and admirably commemorated his achievements—your filial piety could scarcely be greater.

sentences.zh: 尚有五朝聖政盛德，願稽考而繼述之，以揚七廟之光，貽福萬世。

translations.literal: Yet the sagely policies and great virtues of five reigns remain; I urge study and commemoration to burnish the ancestral temples and bless ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sagely policies and great virtues of five reigns still remain. I urge Your Majesty to study and commemorate them, to burnish the glory of the ancestral temples and bless ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 」遷兵、吏二部侍郎，以寶文閣待制知江寧府，徙杭、越州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of War and Personnel, made Academician Attendant of the Hall for Cultivating Literature and Prefect of Jiangning, then transferred to Hangzhou and Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of both the Ministries of War and Personnel, appointed Academician Attendant of the Hall for Cultivating Literature and Prefect of Jiangning, then transferred to Hangzhou and Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 初，浩還朝，帝首及諫立后事，獎歎再三，詢諫草安在。

translations.literal: When Hao first returned to court, the emperor immediately brought up his memorial opposing the empress, praised him repeatedly, and asked where the draft was.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao first returned to court, the emperor immediately brought up his memorial opposing the empress's enthronement, praised him repeatedly, and asked where the draft was.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「焚之矣。

translations.literal: He replied: "I burned it."
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "I burned it."

sentences.zh: 」退告陳瓘，瓘曰：「禍其在此乎！

translations.literal: On leaving he told Chen Guan, who said: "Could disaster lie here?
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, he told Chen Guan, who said, "Could this be the seed of disaster?

sentences.zh: 異時姦人妄出一緘，則不可辨矣。

translations.literal: If some villain later produces a forged copy, you cannot prove it false."
translations.idiomatic: If some villain later produces a forged copy, you will be unable to prove it false."

sentences.zh: 」蔡京用事，素忌浩，乃使其黨為偽疏，言劉后殺卓氏而奪其子。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing came to power he resented Hao and had followers forge a memorial claiming Empress Liu murdered Lady Zhuo and stole her child.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing came to power, he had long resented Hao and had his followers forge a memorial claiming that Empress Liu had murdered Lady Zhuo and stolen her child.

sentences.zh: 遂再責衡州別駕，語在《獻湣太子傳》。

translations.literal: He was again demoted to Vice-Prefect of Hengzhou—the account appears in the Biography of Crown Prince Xianmin.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was again demoted to Vice-Prefect of Hengzhou—the full account appears in the Biography of Crown Prince Xianmin.

sentences.zh: 尋竄昭州，五年始得歸。

translations.literal: He was soon exiled to Zhaozhou and returned only after five years.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon exiled further to Zhaozhou and was not able to return until five years had passed.

sentences.zh: 初，浩除諫官，恐貽親憂，欲固辭。

translations.literal: When first appointed remonstrating official, he feared distressing his parents and wished to decline.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was first appointed remonstrating official, he feared causing his parents distress and wanted to decline firmly.

sentences.zh: 母張氏曰：「兒能報國，無愧於公論，吾顧何憂？

translations.literal: His mother Lady Zhang said: "If my son can serve the country without shame before public opinion, what do I have to fear?
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zhang, said, "If my son can serve the country without shame before public opinion, what do I have to fear?

sentences.zh: 」及浩兩謫嶺表，母不易初意。

translations.literal: Even after he was twice exiled to the far south, she never changed her mind."
translations.idiomatic: Even after Hao was twice exiled to the far south, she never changed her mind."

sentences.zh: 稍復直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: He was eventually restored as Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually restored as Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 瘴疾作，危甚。

translations.literal: He was stricken with miasmic fevers and grew gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: He was stricken with the miasmic fevers of the south and grew gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 楊時過常，往省之。

translations.literal: Yang Shi was passing through Changzhou and went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi was passing through Changzhou and went to visit him.

sentences.zh: 苶然僅存餘息，猶眷眷以國事為問，語不及私。

translations.literal: Emaciated and barely clinging to life, he still asked earnestly after state affairs and spoke not of private matters.
translations.idiomatic: He was emaciated and barely clinging to life, yet he still asked earnestly after affairs of state and spoke not a word of personal matters.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，詔曰：「浩在元符間，任諫爭，危言讜論，朝野推仰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, an edict declared: "During the Yuanfu era Hao served as remonstrating official, speaking blunt truths that won respect at court and in the country."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, an edict declared, "During the Yuanfu era, Hao served as a remonstrating official, speaking blunt truths that won the respect of court and country alike."

sentences.zh: 」復其待制，又贈寶文閣直學士，賜諡「忠」。

translations.literal: His Hanlin status was restored; he was posthumously granted Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature with the posthumous name Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: His status as Hanlin Academician was restored, and he was posthumously granted the title of Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 浩所與遊田晝、王回、曾誕，皆良士也。

translations.literal: Among Hao's friends were Tian Zhou, Wang Hui, and Zeng Yan—all men of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Among Hao's friends were Tian Zhou, Wang Hui, and Zeng Yan—all men of integrity.

sentences.zh: 晝，字承君，陽翟人。

translations.literal: Zhou, courtesy name Chengjun, was a native of Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, courtesy name Chengjun, was a native of Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 樞密使況之從子，以任為校書郎。

translations.literal: A nephew of Council Vice Commissioner Kuang Zhi, he entered service as Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: A nephew of the Council Vice Commissioner Kuang Zhi, he entered service as a Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 調磁州錄事參軍，知西河縣，有善政，民甚德之。

translations.literal: Assigned as recorder in Cizhou and later magistrate of Xihe County, his enlightened policies earned the people's deep gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as recorder in Cizhou and later served as magistrate of Xihe County, where his enlightened policies earned the people's deep gratitude.

sentences.zh: 議論慨慷，有前輩風。

translations.literal: His opinions were bold and forthright, in the manner of earlier generations.
translations.idiomatic: His opinions were bold and forthright, in the manner of the great men of earlier generations.

sentences.zh: 與鄒浩以氣節相激勵。

translations.literal: He and Zou Hao inspired each other with shared moral courage.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zou Hao inspired each other with their shared moral courage.

sentences.zh: 元符中，浩為諫官，晝監京城門，往見浩曰：「平生與君相許者何如，今君為何官？

translations.literal: During the Yuanfu era, while Hao was remonstrating official and Zhou supervised the capital gates, Zhou asked: "What did we promise each other in life? What office do you hold now?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era, while Hao served as remonstrating official and Zhou supervised the capital gates, Zhou visited him and asked, "What did we promise each other in our lifetimes? What office do you hold now?"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「上遇群臣，未嘗假以辭色，獨於浩差若相喜。

translations.literal: Hao said: "The emperor never shows warmth to ministers—yet he seems almost fond of me.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "The emperor never shows warmth to his ministers—yet he seems almost fond of me.

sentences.zh: 天下事固不勝言，意欲待深相信而後發，貴有益也。

translations.literal: State affairs are too grim to recount; I mean to wait until he trusts me fully before speaking, so my words may do good.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of state are too grim to recount. I mean to wait until he trusts me fully before speaking out, so that my words may do some good."

sentences.zh: 」晝然之。

translations.literal: Zhou agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而以病歸許，邸狀報立后，晝謂人曰：「志完不言，可以絕交矣。

translations.literal: Later Zhou returned to Xu on illness; when reports announced the empress's enthronement, Zhou said: "If Zhiwan does not speak out, I will break off our friendship."
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou returned to Xu on account of illness. When courier reports arrived announcing the enthronement of the empress, Zhou told others, "If Zhiwan does not speak out, I will break off our friendship."

sentences.zh: 」浩得罪，晝迎諸塗。

translations.literal: When Hao was punished, Zhou went out to meet him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was punished, Zhou went out to meet him on the road.

sentences.zh: 浩出涕，晝正色責曰：「使志完隱默官京師，遇寒疾不汗，五日死矣。

translations.literal: Hao wept, but Zhou sternly rebuked him: "If you had kept silent in the capital, you would have died within five days of a chill that never broke into sweat.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wept, but Zhou sternly rebuked him: "If you had kept silent and stayed at your post in the capital, you would have died within five days of a chill that never broke into sweat.

sentences.zh: 豈獨嶺海之外能死人哉？

translations.literal: Do you think only exile beyond the mountains and sea can kill a man?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think only exile beyond the mountains and sea can kill a man?

sentences.zh: 願君毋以此舉自滿，士所當為者，未止此也。

translations.literal: Do not congratulate yourself on this one act—a gentleman's duty does not end here.
translations.idiomatic: Do not congratulate yourself on this one act—a gentleman's duty does not end here."

sentences.zh: 」浩茫然自失，歎謝曰：「君之贈我厚矣。」

translations.literal: Hao was stunned and abashed; sighing, he apologized: "Your counsel has been generous indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Hao was stunned and abashed. Sighing, he apologized: "Your counsel to me has been generous indeed."

sentences.zh: 建中靖國初，入為大宗正丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong Jingguo era he entered the capital as Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong Jingguo era, he entered the capital as Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 曾布數羅致之，不為屈，欲與提舉常平官，亦辭。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu repeatedly tried to recruit him but Zhou would not yield; offered Superintendent of Ever-Normal Granaries, he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu repeatedly tried to recruit him, but Zhou would not yield; when Zeng offered him the post of Superintendent of Ever-Normal Granaries, he declined that too.

sentences.zh: 請知淮陽軍，歲大疫，日挾醫問病者藥之，遇疾卒。

translations.literal: He requested appointment as Prefect of Huaiyang; when a great epidemic struck, he went out daily with physicians to treat the sick, but fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He requested appointment as Prefect of Huaiyang. When a great epidemic struck that year, he went out daily with physicians to treat the sick, but fell ill himself and died.

sentences.zh: 淮陽人祀以為土神云。

translations.literal: The people of Huaiyang worshipped him as the god of the soil, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: It is said that the people of Huaiyang worshipped him as the earth god.

sentences.zh: 回，字景深，仙遊人。

translations.literal: Hui, styled Jingshen, was a native of Xianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, courtesy name Jingshen, was from Xianyou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調松滋令。

translations.literal: He placed as jinshi and was assigned magistrate of Songzi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Songzi.

sentences.zh: 荊、沔俗用人祭鬼，回捕治甚嚴，其風遂革。

translations.literal: The custom in Jing and Mian was to sacrifice people to ghosts; Hui arrested and punished this with great severity, and the practice was reformed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jing and Mian region it was customary to offer human victims to spirits; Hui cracked down on the practice with great severity until the evil custom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 知鹿邑縣，入為宗正寺簿。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Luyi County, then entered the capital as clerk of the Court of Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as prefect of Luyi County, he was recalled to the capital as a clerk in the Court of Imperial Clan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元符中，葉祖洽薦為睦親宅講書。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfu era, Ye Zuxia recommended him as lecturer at the Office for Kindred of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfu period, Ye Zuxia recommended him to serve as lecturer at the Directorate for Imperial Kin.

sentences.zh: 與鄒浩友善，皇后劉氏立，浩將論之，密告回，回曰：「事寧有大於此者乎？

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Zou Hao; when Empress Liu was enthroned, Hao was about to remonstrate on the matter and secretly informed Hui; Hui said, "Can there be any affair greater than this?"
translations.idiomatic: He was a close friend of Zou Hao; when Empress Liu was installed, Hao planned to speak out against it and confided in Hui privately; Hui asked, "Could any matter be more momentous than this?"

sentences.zh: 子雖有親，然移孝為忠，亦太夫人素志也。」

translations.literal: "Though you have your father, yet turning filial piety into loyalty is also what the Lady Dowager has always wished."
translations.idiomatic: "Though you still have your father, turning filial devotion into loyalty was always your mother's own wish."

sentences.zh: 浩南遷，人莫敢顧。

translations.literal: When Hao was banished to the south, no one dared to attend to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was exiled to the south, no one dared to show him any regard.

sentences.zh: 回斂交遊錢與治裝，往來經理，且慰安其母。

translations.literal: Hui collected money from friends for his travel expenses, went back and forth managing affairs, and also comforted his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Hui gathered funds from their circle of friends to pay for Hao's journey, traveled back and forth to manage his affairs, and comforted his mother as well.

sentences.zh: 邏者以聞，逮詣詔獄，眾為之懼，回居之晏然。

translations.literal: An informer reported this; he was arrested and taken to the imperial prison; the crowd feared for him, but Hui remained entirely at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Someone nearby reported what he had done; he was seized and brought to the imperial prison, and though many feared for him, Hui remained perfectly calm.

sentences.zh: 御史詰之，對曰：「實嘗預議，不敢欺也。

translations.literal: The censor interrogated him; he replied, "I did indeed take part in the discussion; I dare not deceive."
translations.idiomatic: When the censor questioned him, he answered, "I truly did take part in the deliberation, and I dare not lie about it."

sentences.zh: 」因誦浩所上章，幾二千言。

translations.literal: He then recited the memorial Hao had submitted, nearly two thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited the memorial Hao had submitted, which ran to nearly two thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 獄上，除名停廢。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted, he was stripped of his name and suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported upward, he was removed from the rolls and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 即徒步出都門，行數十里，其子追及，問以家事，不答。

translations.literal: He then walked out of the capital gate; after traveling several tens of li, his son caught up with him and asked about family affairs, but he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately left the capital on foot; after he had gone several dozen li, his son caught up with him and asked about household matters, but he gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 祖洽亦坐黜。

translations.literal: Zuxia was also dismissed for his connection to the case.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxia was dismissed from office as well.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，召還舊官，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Hui was recalled to his former post and promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne, Hui was recalled to his former position and promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 數日卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: Several days later he died, at the age of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few days later, at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 岑象求、王覿、賈易上章，乞錄其子，恤其家，以獎勸忠義。

translations.literal: Cen Xiangqiu, Wang Di, and Jia Yi submitted memorials asking that his son be enrolled in office, his family given relief, to reward and encourage loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Xiangqiu, Wang Di, and Jia Yi submitted memorials asking that his son be given an official appointment and his family be granted relief, so as to reward and encourage loyal conduct.

sentences.zh: 詔除子渙老郊社齋郎，蔡京為相，奪之，仍列名黨籍。

translations.literal: An edict appointed his son Huan as an elder ceremonial attendant at the suburban altars; when Cai Jing became chief minister, this was taken away, and Hui's name was still placed on the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed his son Huan as a ceremonial attendant at the suburban altars, but after Cai Jing became chief councillor the appointment was revoked and Hui's name was entered on the proscribed faction list.

sentences.zh: 曾誕

translations.literal: Zeng Dan
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Dan

translations.literal: (Supplement)
translations.idiomatic: (Supplement)

sentences.zh: 誕，公亮從孫也。

translations.literal: Dan was a grandnephew of Gongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was a grandnephew of Zeng Gongliang.

sentences.zh: 孟后之廢，誕三與浩書，勸力請復后，浩不報。

translations.literal: When Empress Meng was deposed, Dan three times wrote to Hao urging him to press hard for her restoration; Hao did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Meng was deposed, Dan wrote to Hao three times urging him to petition vigorously for her restoration, but Hao never answered.

sentences.zh: 及浩以言南遷，誕著《玉山主人對客問》以譏之，其略曰：「客問：『鄒浩可以為有道之士乎？

translations.literal: When Hao was banished to the south for his words, Dan wrote The Host of Jade Mountain Answers a Guest's Questions to ridicule him; its gist reads: "The guest asked, 'Can Zou Hao be considered a man of the Way?'"
translations.idiomatic: After Hao was exiled to the south for his remonstrance, Dan composed Jade Mountain Host Answers a Guest's Questions to mock him; it begins roughly as follows: "The guest asked, 'Can Zou Hao be regarded as a man of moral wisdom?'"

sentences.zh: 』主人曰：『浩安得為知道。

translations.literal: The host said, "How could Hao be called one who knows the Way?"
translations.idiomatic: The host replied, "How could Hao be said to understand the Way?"

sentences.zh: 雖然，予於此時議浩，是天下無全人也。

translations.literal: Even so, for me to judge Hao at this moment is to say that no one in the world is whole.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, for me to pass judgment on Hao at such a time would be to imply that no one under heaven is without flaw.

sentences.zh: 言之尚足為來世戒。

translations.literal: What is said here may still serve as a warning to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, what follows is still worth offering as a warning to future generations.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「知幾其神乎？

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, "Is knowing the subtle signs not divine?"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Is not discerning the first signs of change truly numinous?"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「知進退存亡而不失其正者，其惟聖人乎？

translations.literal: It also says, "Is not he who knows advance and retreat, survival and extinction, yet never loses what is right, none other than the sage?"
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Is not the sage alone he who knows when to advance or withdraw, live or perish, yet never forsakes what is right?"

sentences.zh: 」方孟后之廢，人莫不知劉氏之將立，至四年之後而冊命未行，是天子知清議之足畏也。

translations.literal: When Empress Meng was deposed, everyone knew the Liu clan would be enthroned; yet four years passed before the investiture was carried out—this showed the Son of Heaven knew how much pure criticism was to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Meng was deposed, everyone knew Empress Liu would succeed her, yet four years passed before the formal investiture was issued, which shows the emperor understood how formidable pure public opinion could be.

sentences.zh: 使當其時，浩力言復后，能感悟天子，則無今日劉氏之事，貽朝廷於過舉，再三言而不聽，則義亦當矣。

translations.literal: Had Hao at that time pressed hard for the empress's restoration and moved the Son of Heaven to understand, there would have been no Liu affair today; burdening the court with a mistaken act, if after speaking again and again he was not heeded, then righteousness was fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: If at that time Hao had argued forcefully for restoring the empress and persuaded the emperor, the Liu affair would never have occurred; having repeatedly remonstrated without being heard, he had already fulfilled his moral duty even if the court was left with a grievous mistake.

sentences.zh: 使是時得罪，必不若是酷以貽老母之憂矣。

translations.literal: Had he incurred offense at that time, it would surely not have been so cruel as to bring grief to his old mother.
translations.idiomatic: Had he fallen afoul of the throne then, the punishment would surely not have been so harsh as to burden his aged mother with such grief.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 若浩者，雖不得為知幾之士，然百世之下，頑夫廉，懦夫有立志，尚不失為聖人 之清也。

translations.literal: A man like Hao, though he cannot be called one who knows subtle signs, yet a hundred generations hence may make the shameless honest and the timid resolute—he still does not fall short of the sage's purity.
translations.idiomatic: A man like Hao may not qualify as one who discerns the subtle turn of events, yet even a hundred generations from now he may still make the shameless honest and the timid resolute, and he does not fall short of the moral clarity of the sages.

sentences.zh: 』」其書既出，識者或以比韓愈《諫臣論》。

translations.literal: When the book appeared, discerning readers sometimes compared it to Han Yu's On Remonstrating Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the work appeared, thoughtful readers sometimes compared it to Han Yu's Essay on Remonstrating Ministers.

sentences.zh: 誕仕亦不顯。

translations.literal: Dan's official career was also undistinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's own career in office was likewise unremarkable.

sentences.zh: 陳瓘，字瑩中，南劍州沙縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Guan, styled Yingzhong, was a native of Shaxian in Nanjian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan, courtesy name Yingzhong, was a native of Shaxian in Nanjian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，不喜為進取學。

translations.literal: From youth he loved reading and did not care for study aimed at advancement.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved reading and had no taste for the sort of learning pursued for career advancement.

sentences.zh: 父母勉以門戶事，乃應舉，一出中甲科。

translations.literal: His parents urged him on behalf of the family line, so he entered the examinations and at his first attempt passed with highest honors in the jinshi class.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents pressed him for the family's sake, he entered the examinations and passed the jinshi on his first attempt at the top of his class.

sentences.zh: 調湖州掌書記，簽書越州判官。

translations.literal: He was assigned as secretary at Huzhou and as assistant magistrate at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed recording secretary at Huzhou and assistant magistrate at Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 守蔡卞察其賢，每事加禮，而瓘測知其心術，常欲遠之，屢引疾求歸，章不得上。

translations.literal: Prefect Cai Bian noticed his worth and treated him with special deference in every matter, but Guan fathomed his intentions and always wished to keep his distance; he repeatedly pleaded illness to return home, but his memorials could not be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Cai Bian saw his talent and treated him with exceptional courtesy, but Guan discerned Bian's underlying motives and constantly sought to keep away from him; he repeatedly asked to resign on grounds of illness, yet his petitions never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 檄攝通判明州。

translations.literal: He was ordered by dispatch to serve as vice-prefect of Mingzhou in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned by official dispatch to serve as acting vice-prefect of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卞素敬道人張懷素，謂非世間人，時且來越，卞留瓘小須之，瓘不肯止，曰：「子不語怪力亂神，斯近怪矣。

translations.literal: Bian had always revered the Daoist Zhang Huaisu, declaring him no ordinary man of the world; when the latter was about to come to Yue, Bian asked Guan to wait a little; Guan refused to stay and said, "The Master said nothing of prodigies, force, disorder, or spirits—this comes close to the prodigious."
translations.idiomatic: Bian had long revered the Daoist Zhang Huaisu and called him no ordinary mortal; when Huaisu was about to visit Yue, Bian asked Guan to stay a little longer, but Guan would not and said, "Confucius said nothing of strange powers, violence, disorder, or spirits—this is perilously close to the strange."

sentences.zh: 州牧既信重，民將從風而靡。

translations.literal: Since the prefect already believed and honored him, the people would follow the wind and fall in line.
translations.idiomatic: Once the prefect trusts and honors such a man, the people will follow suit as if swept by the wind.

sentences.zh: 不識之，未為不幸也。

translations.literal: Not to recognize him is no misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing him would be no misfortune at all.

sentences.zh: 」後二十年而懷素誅。

translations.literal: Twenty years later Huaisu was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years later, Huaisu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 明州職田之入厚，瓘不取，盡棄於官以歸。

translations.literal: The income from Mingzhou's official fields was substantial; Guan did not take it and surrendered all of it to the government before returning home.
translations.idiomatic: The income from Ming Prefecture's official land was considerable, but Guan took none of it and returned the whole amount to the government before going home.

sentences.zh: 章惇入相，瓘從眾道謁。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun entered the chancellorship, Guan went with the crowd to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun became chief councillor, Guan joined the throng in paying a courtesy call.

sentences.zh: 惇聞其名，獨邀與同載，詢當世之務，瓘曰：「請以所乘舟為喻：偏重可行乎？
