translations.literal: Dun, hearing his name, invited him alone to ride in the same carriage and asked about affairs of the age; Guan said, "Please take the boat we are riding as a metaphor: can it sail when heavily weighted on one side?"
translations.idiomatic: Dun had heard of him and invited him alone to share his carriage, asking his views on current affairs; Guan replied, "Let me use this boat we are in as an analogy: can a boat that lists heavily to one side keep going?"

sentences.zh: 移左置右，其偏一也。

translations.literal: Move the weight from left to right, and the imbalance is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Shift the weight from the left side to the right, and the list is just the same.

sentences.zh: 明此，則可行矣。

translations.literal: Understand this, and then it can proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Once this is understood, the boat can sail safely.

sentences.zh: 天子待公為政，敢問將何先？

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven expects you to govern; may I ask what you will put first?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is counting on you to govern; dare I ask what you intend to take up first?

sentences.zh: 」惇曰：「司馬光姦邪，所當先辨，勢無急於此。

translations.literal: Dun said, "Sima Guang is treacherous and corrupt; this must be clarified first—nothing is more urgent."
translations.idiomatic: Dun replied, "Sima Guang is wicked and corrupt; that must be settled first, and nothing is more pressing."

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「公誤矣。

translations.literal: Guan said, "You are mistaken, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Guan said, "You are mistaken."

sentences.zh: 此猶欲平舟勢而移左以置右，果然，將失天下之望。

translations.literal: This is still like trying to right a listing boat by moving weight from left to right; if that is done, you will lose the hope of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That is still like trying to steady a listing boat by shifting weight from left to right; if you do that, you will forfeit the trust of the empire.

sentences.zh: 」惇厲色曰：「光不務纘述先烈，而大改成緒，誤國如此，非姦邪而何？

translations.literal: Dun said sternly, "Guang did not devote himself to continuing the work of the former sage-emperor, but instead greatly altered established order and misled the state like this—if that is not treachery and wickedness, what is?"
translations.idiomatic: Dun's face darkened as he said, "Guang did not seek to carry on the legacy of the late emperor but instead overturned established policy and harmed the state so gravely—if that is not wicked treachery, what is?"

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「不察其心而疑其跡，則不為無罪；

translations.literal: Guan said, "If one does not examine his mind but only suspects his tracks, that is not without fault;"
translations.idiomatic: Guan replied, "Failing to discern his intentions while condemning his actions would not be entirely without fault;"

sentences.zh: 若指為姦邪，又復改作，則誤國益甚矣。

translations.literal: but if one calls him treacherous and wicked and then reverses policy again, the harm to the state will be even greater.
translations.idiomatic: but if you denounce him as wicked and treacherous and then reverse course once more, the harm to the state will be far worse.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，唯消朋黨，持中道，庶可以救弊。

translations.literal: For the present plan, only by dissolving factional cliques and holding to the middle way can abuses perhaps be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: The course for today is to dissolve partisan cliques and hold to the middle path; only then might the state's ills be remedied.

sentences.zh: 」意雖忤惇，然亦驚異，頗有兼收之語。

translations.literal: Though his meaning went against Dun, Dun was also startled and admiring, and spoke somewhat of encompassing both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Though his words offended Dun, Dun was also astonished and spoke with some hint of willingness to accommodate opposing views.

sentences.zh: 至都，用為太學博士。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital, he was appointed erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After he reached the capital, he was appointed an erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 會卞與惇合志，正論遂絀。

translations.literal: When Bian and Dun united in purpose, straight discourse was suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian and Dun joined forces, honest political debate was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 卞黨薛昂、林自官學省，議毀《資治通鑒》，瓘因策士題引神宗所製序文以問，昂、自意沮。

translations.literal: Bian's faction-members Xue Ang and Lin Zi held posts in the Directorate of Education and proposed to denounce the Comprehensive Mirror; Guan, in an examination question for scholars, cited the preface written by Emperor Shenzong to challenge them, and Ang and Zi lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's allies Xue Ang and Lin Zi, holding posts in the Directorate of Education, proposed to denounce the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government; Guan framed an examination question quoting the preface written by Shenzong, and Ang and Zi were deterred.

sentences.zh: 御史龔夬擊蔡京，朝廷將逐夬，瓘言：「紹聖以來，七年五逐言者，常安民、孫諤、董敦逸、陳次升、鄒浩五人者，皆與京異議而去。

translations.literal: Censor Gong Mie attacked Cai Jing; the court was about to dismiss Mie; Guan said, "Since Shaosheng, in seven years five remonstrators have been driven out—Chang Anmin, Sun E, Dong Dunyi, Chen Cisheng, and Zou Hao—all left because they differed with Jing."
translations.idiomatic: When investigating censor Gong Mie attacked Cai Jing and the court was poised to oust Mie, Guan said, "Since the Shaosheng era, five outspoken officials have been driven out in seven years—Chang Anmin, Sun E, Dong Dunyi, Chen Cisheng, and Zou Hao—all dismissed for disagreeing with Jing."

sentences.zh: 今又罷夬，將若公道何。

translations.literal: Now Mie is to be dismissed again—what will become of public fairness?
translations.idiomatic: Now that Mie is to be dismissed as well, what is left of fairness at court?

sentences.zh: 」遂草疏論京，未及上，時皇太后已歸政，瓘言外戚向宗良兄弟與侍從希寵之士交通，使物議籍籍，謂皇太后今猶預政。

translations.literal: He then drafted a memorial criticizing Jing; before it could be submitted, the Empress Dowager had already returned power; Guan spoke of the empress's kin, the Xiang Zongliang brothers, mingling with attendants and office-seekers, causing public opinion to buzz that the Empress Dowager still intervened in government.
translations.idiomatic: He then drafted a memorial attacking Jing, but before he could submit it the Empress Dowager had already returned power to the throne; Guan spoke of how the empress's relatives, the Xiang Zongliang brothers, consorted with courtiers seeking favor, stirring widespread talk that the Empress Dowager still meddled in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 由是罷監揚州糧料院。

translations.literal: For this he was removed from his post as superintendent of the Yangzhou grain depot.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was dismissed from his post as superintendent of the Yangzhou grain depot.

sentences.zh: 瓘出都門，繳四章奏之，並明宣仁誣謗事。

translations.literal: Guan left the capital gate and submitted four memorials on the way, also clarifying the slander against Empress Xuanren.
translations.idiomatic: As Guan left the capital, he submitted four memorials along the way, also setting forth the false charges made against Empress Xuanren.

sentences.zh: 帝密遣使賜以黃金百兩，后亦命勿遽去，畀十僧牒為行裝，改知無為軍。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly sent an envoy to bestow a hundred taels of gold; the empress also ordered him not to leave hastily and gave him ten monk ordination certificates for travel expenses, and he was reassigned as military commissioner of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent an envoy to grant him a hundred taels of gold; the empress also told him not to depart in haste and gave him ten ordination certificates for monks as travel funds, and he was reassigned to govern Wuwei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年，還為著作郎，遷右司員外郎兼權給事中。

translations.literal: The next year he returned as drafting secretary and was promoted to assistant director in the right office and acting chief of the Requisite Office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as a drafting secretary and promoted to assistant director in the Right Office, concurrently serving as acting chief remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 宰相曾布使客告以將即真，瓘語子正彙曰：「吾與丞相議事多不合，今若此，是欲以官爵相餌也。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zeng Bu sent a guest to inform him that he would soon receive formal appointment; Guan told his son Zheng Hui, "My views often differ from the Chancellor's; now that it comes to this, he means to bait me with rank and salary."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Zeng Bu sent an intermediary to tell him he was about to receive a formal appointment; Guan said to his son Zheng Hui, "I have often disagreed with the Chancellor on policy; this gesture is plainly an attempt to buy me off with office and rank."

sentences.zh: 若受其薦進，復有異同，則公議私恩，兩有愧矣。

translations.literal: If I accept his recommendation and later differ again, I shall be ashamed before both public opinion and private obligation.
translations.idiomatic: If I accept his patronage and then disagree with him again, I shall be compromised both in public duty and in private gratitude.

sentences.zh: 吾有一書論其過，將投之以決去就，汝其書之。

translations.literal: I have a letter setting forth his faults which I shall submit to decide whether I stay or go—you shall copy it.
translations.idiomatic: I have written a letter detailing his faults, which I mean to submit to settle whether I stay or leave; you shall make a fair copy.

sentences.zh: 但郊祀不遠，彼不相容，則澤不及汝矣，能不介於心乎？

translations.literal: But the suburban sacrifice is not far off; if he cannot tolerate me, the favor will not reach you—can you remain unconcerned?
translations.idiomatic: But the suburban sacrifice is near; if he cannot abide me, the benefits will never reach you—can you truly keep that from weighing on your mind?

sentences.zh: 」正彙願得書。

translations.literal: Zheng Hui asked to have the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hui asked to see the letter.

sentences.zh: 旦持入省，布使數人邀相見，甫就席，遽出書，布大怒，爭辯移時，至箕踞誶語，瓘色不為動，徐起白曰：「適所論者國事，是非有公議，公未可失待士禮。

translations.literal: The next morning he brought it into the ministry; Bu sent several men to invite him to a meeting; as soon as he took his seat he promptly produced the letter; Bu flew into a rage and argued for a long time, even sitting with legs spread and hurling abuse; Guan's countenance did not change; he rose slowly and said, "What we have just discussed concerns state affairs; right and wrong belong to public judgment—you ought not to abandon the courtesy due a gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he brought it to the ministry; Bu sent several men to invite him to meet; scarcely had he taken his seat when he produced the letter; Bu flew into a rage and argued for a long time, even sitting sprawled and hurling abuse; Guan remained unmoved, rose calmly, and said, "What we have been discussing is a matter of state; right and wrong are for public judgment to decide, and you must not abandon the respect owed a gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」布矍然改容。

translations.literal: Bu started in astonishment and changed his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Bu started in shock and immediately changed his manner.

sentences.zh: 信宿，出知泰州。

translations.literal: Two nights later he was sent out to govern Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he was sent out to serve as prefect of Ta Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，除名竄袁州、廉州，移郴州，稍復宣德郎。

translations.literal: During Chongning he was struck from the rolls and banished to Yuanzhou and Lianzhou, then moved to Chenzhou, and was later restored somewhat to the post of Gentleman for Manifest Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era he was struck from the official rolls and exiled first to Yuan and Lian Prefectures, then transferred to Chen Prefecture, and was later partially restored to the rank of Gentleman for Manifest Virtue.

sentences.zh: 正彙在杭，告蔡京有動搖東宮跡。

translations.literal: Zheng Hui was in Hangzhou and reported that Cai Jing showed signs of undermining the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: While in Hangzhou, Zheng Hui reported that Cai Jing was acting in ways that threatened the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 杭守蔡薿執送京師，先飛書告京俾為計。

translations.literal: Hangzhou prefect Cai Wei had him seized and sent to the capital, first dispatching a letter to inform Jing so he could prepare countermeasures.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Hangzhou, Cai Wei, had him arrested and sent to the capital, first dispatching an urgent letter to Jing so he could prepare his response.

sentences.zh: 事下開封府制獄，並逮瓘。

translations.literal: The case was handed to the Kaifeng prefecture for an inquisition, and Guan was arrested as well.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Kaifeng prefectural prison for investigation, and Guan was arrested too.

sentences.zh: 尹李孝稱逼使證其妄，瓘曰：「正彙聞京將不利社稷，傳於道路，瓘豈得預知？

translations.literal: Prefect Li Xiaocheng pressed him to testify that the report was false; Guan said, "Zheng Hui heard that Jing would harm the altars of state and the report spread along the roads—how could Guan have known beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Li Xiaocheng pressed him to testify that the accusation was false; Guan replied, "Zheng Hui heard rumors that Jing would harm the state, and those rumors were everywhere on the road—how could I have known that in advance?"

sentences.zh: 以所不知，忘父子之恩而指其為妄，則情有所不忍；

translations.literal: To declare false what I do not know, forgetting the debt between father and son, my feelings cannot bear it;
translations.idiomatic: To call it false on the basis of what I do not know, forgetting the bond between father and son, is more than my heart can bear;

sentences.zh: 挾私情以符合其說，又義所不為。

translations.literal: yet to indulge private feeling in order to fit their story is also what righteousness forbids.
translations.idiomatic: yet to let private feeling bend my testimony to suit their account is also what duty forbids.

sentences.zh: 京之姦邪，必為國禍。

translations.literal: Jing's treachery and wickedness will surely become a national calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's wicked treachery is bound to bring disaster upon the state.

sentences.zh: 瓘固嘗論之於諫省，亦不待今日語言間也。

translations.literal: Guan had already criticized this in the remonstrance office; there is no need to wait until today's conversation.
translations.idiomatic: I had already made that case in the remonstrance office; I need hardly wait until today to say it.

sentences.zh: 」內侍黃經臣蒞鞫，聞其辭，失聲歎息，謂曰：「主上正欲得實，但如言以對可也。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Huang Jingchen presided at the interrogation; hearing his words he cried out in sigh and said, "His Majesty wants only the truth—simply answer as you have spoken."
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendant Huang Jingchen presided at the hearing; hearing Guan's words, he exclaimed in admiration and said, "His Majesty wants only the truth; you need only answer as you have just spoken."

sentences.zh: 」獄具，正彙猶以所告失實流海上，瓘亦安置通州。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, Zheng Hui was still exiled to the sea coast for the unreality of his report, and Guan was also assigned to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was closed, Zheng Hui was still banished to the coastal exile for reporting what proved untrue, and Guan was relegated to Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瓘嘗著《尊堯集》，謂紹聖史官專據王安石《日錄》改修《神宗史》，變亂是非，不可傳信；

translations.literal: Guan once wrote the Collection in Honor of Yao, holding that Shaosheng historiographers relied solely on Wang Anshi's Daily Records to revise the History of Emperor Shenzong, inverting right and wrong so that it could not be trusted;
translations.idiomatic: Guan had written the Collection in Honor of Yao, arguing that under Shaosheng the historiographers had revised the History of Emperor Shenzong relying solely on Wang Anshi's Daily Records, distorting truth and falsehood so that the record could not be trusted;

sentences.zh: 深明誣妄，以正君臣之義。

translations.literal: it deeply exposed falsehood and calumny to set right the ethics between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: it thoroughly exposed falsehood and slander in order to restore the proper ethics of ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 張商英為相，取其書，既上，而商英罷，瓘又徙台州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shangying became chief minister he took the book; after it was submitted Shangying was dismissed, and Guan was again transferred to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shangying became chief councillor he seized the book; after it was submitted Shangying was dismissed, and Guan was transferred again to Ta Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰相遍令所過州出兵甲護送；

translations.literal: The chief minister ordered every prefecture he passed through to dispatch armed men to escort him;
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillor ordered every prefecture along the route to dispatch armed guards to escort him;

sentences.zh: 至台，每十日一徙告；

translations.literal: upon reaching Taizhou, he was moved every ten days under notice of transfer;
translations.idiomatic: once he reached Taizhou, he was transferred every ten days at official notice;

sentences.zh: 且命凶人石悈知州事，執至庭，大陳獄具，將脅以死。

translations.literal: and the violent man Shi Ke was appointed to govern the prefecture; he had Guan brought to the hall, laid out the completed case in full, and intended to intimidate him with death.
translations.idiomatic: and the notorious Shi Ke was put in charge of the prefecture; Guan was brought before the court, the full dossier of the case was displayed, and they intended to terrify him with the threat of death.

sentences.zh: 瓘揣知其意，大呼曰：「今日之事，豈被制旨邪！

translations.literal: Guan fathomed their intent and cried out, "Today's affair—was it ordered by imperial edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan saw through their intent and shouted, "Was today's proceeding carried out under an imperial directive!"

sentences.zh: 」悈失措，始告之曰：「朝廷令取《尊堯集》爾。

translations.literal: Ke lost composure and then told him, "The court only ordered the Collection in Honor of Yao to be seized."
translations.idiomatic: Ke was thrown off balance and then told him, "The court only ordered the Collection in Honor of Yao to be taken."

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「然則何用許。

translations.literal: Guan said, "Then what need for all this?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan said, "Then what was all this theatrics for?"

sentences.zh: 使君知『尊堯』所以立名乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Honor know why it was called 'In Honor of Yao'?
translations.idiomatic: Do you understand why the collection was given the name 'In Honor of Yao'?

sentences.zh: 蓋以神考為堯，主上為舜，助舜尊堯，何得為罪？

translations.literal: For it treats Shenzong as Yao and the present sovereign as Shun, helping Shun honor Yao—how can that be a crime?
translations.idiomatic: The title takes Emperor Shenzong for Yao and the reigning sovereign for Shun, and means to help Shun honor Yao—how can that be a crime?

sentences.zh: 時相學術淺短，為人所愚。

translations.literal: The chief minister's learning is shallow and narrow, and he is deluded by others.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister's scholarship is shallow and narrow, and he lets himself be played for a fool.

sentences.zh: 君所得幾何，乃亦不畏公議，干犯名分乎？

translations.literal: Sir, how much do you stand to gain, that you also do not fear public opinion and violate proper status between sovereign and subject?
translations.idiomatic: What can you possibly gain from this, that you would brazenly defy public opinion and violate the rightful order between ruler and subject?

sentences.zh: 」悈慚，揖使退。

translations.literal: Yue, ashamed, bowed and had him withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, ashamed, bowed and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 所以窘辱之百端，終不能害。

translations.literal: For this reason they harassed and humiliated him by every means, yet in the end could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore tried every means to humiliate and torment him, yet in the end could not harm him.

sentences.zh: 宰相猶以悈為怯而罷之。

translations.literal: The chief minister still deemed Yue cowardly and removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister still judged Yue too timid and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 在台五年，乃得自便。

translations.literal: After five years in Taizhou, he was finally granted free movement.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in Taizhou, he was at last allowed to move about freely.

sentences.zh: 才復承事郎，帝批進目，以為所擬未當，令再敘一官，仍與差遣，執政持不行。

translations.literal: When he was again made Assistant Gentlemen of Attendance, the emperor annotated the advancement roster, holding the proposed rank unsuitable and ordering one further promotion plus an official assignment—the chief administrators blocked it and would not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: When he was restored to Assistant Gentlemen of Attendance, the emperor marked up the advancement list, deeming the proposed rank unsuitable and ordering one further promotion with an official assignment—but those in power blocked it and refused to implement the order.

sentences.zh: 卜居江州，復有譖之者，至不許輒出城。

translations.literal: He chose residence in Jiangzhou; again there were slanderers, to the point that he was not permitted to leave the city at will.
translations.idiomatic: He settled in Jiangzhou, but slanderers soon arose again, and he was forbidden even to leave the city without permission.

sentences.zh: 旋令居南康，才至，又移楚。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to reside in Nankang; he had just arrived when he was moved again to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to move to Nankang, and no sooner had he arrived than he was transferred again to Chu.

sentences.zh: 瓘平生論京、卞，皆披擿其處心，發露其情慝，最所忌恨，故得禍最酷，不使一日少安。

translations.literal: Guan throughout his life, in criticizing Jing and Bian, always exposed their hidden motives and revealed their wicked hearts—what they most hated; therefore he suffered the cruelest calamity and was not granted a single day of ease.
translations.idiomatic: In his attacks on Cai Jing and Cai Bian, Guan had always laid bare their hidden motives and exposed their malice—the very thing they hated most. For that reason he suffered the harshest persecution and was not granted a single day of peace.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Xuanhe, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Xuanhe, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 瓘謙和不與物競，閑居矜莊自持，語不苟發。

translations.literal: Guan was modest and gentle and did not contend with others; in retirement he maintained dignity and self-restraint, and did not speak casually.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was modest and uncontentious; in retirement he held himself with quiet dignity and never spoke lightly.

sentences.zh: 通於《易》，數言國家大事，後多驗。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Book of Changes, repeatedly spoke on great affairs of state, and later many of his words proved true.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the Book of Changes, repeatedly spoke on great affairs of state, and many of his predictions later proved true.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，詔贈諫議大夫，召官正彙。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Remonstrance Grandee and summoned his son Zhenghui to office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, an edict posthumously granted him the title Remonstrance Grandee and summoned his son Zhenghui to office.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十六年，高宗謂輔臣曰：「陳瓘昔為諫官，甚有讜議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Shaoxing, Gaozong said to his chief ministers: "Chen Guan once served as remonstrance official and had many forthright criticisms.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Shaoxing, Gaozong told his chief ministers, "Chen Guan once served as a remonstrance official and offered many forthright criticisms.

sentences.zh: 近覽所著《尊堯集》，明君臣之大分，合於《易》天尊地卑及《春秋》尊王之法。

translations.literal: Recently reading his Respecting Yao Collection, it clarifies the great distinction between sovereign and minister, matching the Change's 'Heaven honored, earth lowly' and the Spring and Autumn Annals' method of honoring the king.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, reading his Respecting Yao Collection, I find it clarifies the great distinction between sovereign and minister, in accord with the Change's principle that Heaven is honored and earth is lowly, and with the Spring and Autumn Annals' law of honoring the king.

sentences.zh: 王安石號通經術，而其言乃謂『道隆德駿者，天子當北面而問焉』，其背經悖理甚矣。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi claimed mastery of the classics, yet his words said, 'Those of elevated Way and eminent virtue—the Son of Heaven should face north and inquire of them'—how greatly he betrayed the classics and violated reason.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi claimed mastery of the classics, yet he wrote that 'those whose Way is lofty and virtue eminent—the Son of Heaven should face north and inquire of them.' That is a profound betrayal of the classics and violation of reason.

sentences.zh: 瓘宜特賜諡以表之。

translations.literal: Guan should be specially granted a posthumous title to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan deserves a special posthumous title to honor him.

sentences.zh: 」諡曰「忠肅」。

translations.literal: The posthumous title was Loyal and Stern.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Loyal and Stern.

sentences.zh: 任伯雨

translations.literal: Ren Boyu
translations.idiomatic: Ren Boyu

sentences.zh: 任伯雨，字德翁，眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Ren Boyu, style name De'eng, was a man of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Boyu, whose style name was De'eng, came from Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 父孜，字遵聖，以學問氣節推重鄉里，名與蘇洵埒，仕至光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: His father Zi, style name Zunsheng, was esteemed in his home district for learning and moral integrity, his fame equal to Su Xun's, and he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zi, style name Zunsheng, was respected throughout the district for learning and moral integrity; his renown matched Su Xun's, and he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其弟伋，字師中，亦知名，嘗通判黃州，後知滬州。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ji, style name Shizhong, was also well known; he once served as Vice-Prefect of Huangzhou and later as prefect of Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ji, style name Shizhong, was also well known; he had served as Vice-Prefect of Huangzhou and later governed Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 當時稱「大任」、「小任」。

translations.literal: They were called at the time Great Ren and Small Ren.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people called them Great Ren and Small Ren.

sentences.zh: 伯雨自幼，已矯然不群，邃經術，文力雄健。

translations.literal: From youth Boyu already stood apart from the crowd, was deeply versed in the classics, and wrote with vigorous force.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Boyu already stood apart from the crowd, was deeply versed in the classics, and wrote with vigorous force.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，調施州清江主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as registrar of Qingjiang in Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was posted as registrar of Qingjiang in Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 郡守檄使蒞公庫，笑曰：「里名勝母，曾子不入，此職何為至我哉？

translations.literal: The prefect ordered him to take charge of the public treasury; he laughed and said: "There is a place called Shengmu—Zengzi would not enter it. Why should this post come to me?
translations.idiomatic: The prefect ordered him to oversee the public treasury. He laughed and said, "There is a place called Shengmu—Victory-over-Mother. Zengzi would not even pass through it. Why should this post come to me?"

sentences.zh: 」拒不受。

translations.literal: He refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 知雍丘縣，御吏如束濕，撫民如傷。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Yongqiu County, he controlled clerks as tightly as binding wet cords and treated the people as if tending wounds.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Yongqiu County, he kept his clerks on as tight a rein as wet cords under tension, and treated the people as one treats an injury.

sentences.zh: 縣枕汴流，漕運不絕，舊苦多盜，然未嘗有獲者，人莫知其故。

translations.literal: The county bordered the Bian River; canal transport never ceased; formerly it suffered many thieves, yet none were ever caught, and no one knew why.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay along the Bian River, where canal traffic never ceased. It had long been plagued by thieves, yet none were ever caught, and no one knew why.

sentences.zh: 伯雨下令網舟無得宿境內，始猶不從，則命東下者斧斷其纜，趣京師者護以出，自是外戶不閉。

translations.literal: Boyu ordered that net-boats could not anchor within the district; at first they did not obey, so he had those heading east have their cables cut with axes, and those bound for the capital escorted out; from then on outer doors were never closed.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu ordered that fishing boats could not anchor overnight within the county. When they at first disobeyed, he had eastbound boats' cables cut with axes and westbound boats escorted out toward the capital. From then on, people no longer locked their outer doors at night.

sentences.zh: 使者上其狀，召為大宗正丞，甫至，擢左正言。

translations.literal: The envoy reported his achievements; he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court; he had scarcely arrived when he was promoted to Left Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy reported his achievements, and he was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court. He had scarcely arrived when he was promoted to Left Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 時徽宗初政，納用讜論，伯雨首擊章惇，曰：「惇久竊朝柄，迷國罔上，毒流搢紳，乘先帝變故倉卒，輒逞異意，睥睨萬乘，不復有臣子之恭。

translations.literal: At the start of Huizong's reign, forthright counsel was welcomed; Boyu was first to strike at Zhang Dun, saying: "Dun long usurped court power, misled the state and deceived the throne, poison spread among the gentry, seizing on the late emperor's sudden crisis he promptly showed contrary intent, eying the imperial seat with contempt, no longer showing a subject's deference.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huizong's reign, forthright counsel was welcomed, and Boyu was the first to attack Zhang Dun. He said, "Dun long usurped control of the court, misled the state and deceived the throne, and spread poison among the gentry. Seizing on the late emperor's sudden crisis, he promptly revealed contrary intent, eying the imperial throne with contempt and no longer showing a subject's deference.

sentences.zh: 向使其計得行，將置陛下與皇太后於何地！

translations.literal: Had his scheme succeeded, where would Your Majesty and the Empress Dowager have been placed!
translations.idiomatic: Had his scheme succeeded, where would Your Majesty and the Empress Dowager have been left?

sentences.zh: 若貸而不誅，則天下大義不明，大法不立矣。

translations.literal: If he is spared and not punished, then the great principles of the realm will be unclear and the great law will not stand.
translations.idiomatic: If he is spared rather than punished, the great principles of the realm will remain unclear and the great law will never stand.

sentences.zh: 臣聞北使言，去年遼主方食，聞中國黜惇，放箸而起，稱甚善者再，謂南朝錯用此人。

translations.literal: I hear from the northern envoy that last year, while the Liao ruler was at his meal, hearing that China had dismissed Dun, he set down his chopsticks and rose, twice praising it as excellent, saying the southern court had wrongly employed this man.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard from the northern envoy that last year, while the Liao ruler was at his meal, he learned that China had dismissed Dun. He set down his chopsticks and rose, twice praising the move as excellent, and said the southern court had long misused this man.

sentences.zh: 北使又問，何為只若是行遣？

translations.literal: The northern envoy also asked: why was he only dealt with in this manner?
translations.idiomatic: The northern envoy also asked why Dun had been dealt with only in this mild fashion.

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，不獨孟子所謂「國人皆曰可殺」，雖蠻貊之邦，莫不以為可殺也。

translations.literal: From this we see—not only what Mencius called 'the whole state says he may be killed'—even barbarian lands all think he should be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this, it is not only what Mencius meant when he said 'the whole state says he may be killed'—even barbarian lands all hold that he should be killed.

sentences.zh: 」章八上，貶惇雷州。

translations.literal: Eight memorials submitted; Dun was demoted to Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted eight memorials in all, and Dun was banished to Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 繼論蔡卞六大罪，語在《卞傳》。

translations.literal: He then argued Cai Bian's six great crimes—the account is in the Biography of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out Cai Bian's six great crimes—the full account appears in the Biography of Bian.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國改元，當國者欲和調元祐、紹聖之人，故以「中」為名。

translations.literal: When the era was changed to Jianzhong Jingguo, those in power wished to reconcile men of the Yuanyou and Shaosheng factions, hence naming it with center.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign era was changed to Jianzhong Jingguo, those in power wished to reconcile men of the Yuanyou and Shaosheng factions, and so took center for its name.

sentences.zh: 伯雨言：「人才固不當分黨與，然自古未有君子小人雜然並進可以致治者。

translations.literal: Boyu said: "Talent should not be divided by faction, yet since antiquity there has never been a case where gentlemen and petty men were mixed together in advancement and good governance resulted.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu said, "Talent should not be divided by faction, yet since antiquity there has never been a case where gentlemen and petty men advanced together and good governance resulted.

sentences.zh: 蓋君子易退，小人難退，二者並用，終於君子盡去，小人獨留。

translations.literal: For gentlemen easily withdraw while petty men are hard to remove; when both are employed together, it ends with gentlemen all gone and petty men alone remaining.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen withdraw easily, but petty men are hard to remove. When both are employed together, the end is always the same: the gentlemen are gone and the petty men alone remain.

sentences.zh: 唐德宗坐此致播遷之禍，『建中』乃其紀號，不可以不戒。」

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong of Tang suffered exile because of this; Jianzhong was his era name—this cannot but serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong of Tang suffered exile for just this reason, and Jianzhong was his era name. That cannot but serve as a warning."

sentences.zh: 時議者欲西北典郡專用武臣，伯雨謂：「李林甫致祿山之亂者，此也。

translations.literal: At the time debaters wished northwest frontier prefectures to employ military men exclusively; Boyu said: "This is what Li Linfu did to bring on An Lushan's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some argued that northwest frontier prefectures should be entrusted exclusively to military men. Boyu said, "This is precisely what Li Linfu did to bring on An Lushan's rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」又論鍾傅、王贍生湟、鄯邊事，失與國心，宜棄其地，以安邊息民；

translations.literal: He also argued on the frontier affairs of Zhong Fu and Wang Shan in Huang and Shan—their policy lost accord with the state's heart; the territories should be abandoned to settle the frontier and give the people rest;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that in the Huang and Shan frontier affairs involving Zhong Fu and Wang Shan, policy had lost touch with the state's true interests, and that those territories should be abandoned to settle the frontier and give the people rest;

sentences.zh: 張耒、黃庭堅、晁補之、歐陽棐、劉唐老等宜在朝廷。

translations.literal: Zhang Lei, Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi, Ouyang Fei, Liu Tanglao and others should be at court.
translations.idiomatic: and that Zhang Lei, Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi, Ouyang Fei, Liu Tanglao, and others should be recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 上書皇太后，乞暴蔡京之惡，召還陳瓘，以全定策之勳。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial to the Empress Dowager, begging that Cai Jing's wickedness be exposed and Chen Guan recalled, to complete the merit of the enthronement decision.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the Empress Dowager, begging that Cai Jing's wickedness be exposed and Chen Guan recalled, so that the merit of the enthronement decision might be made whole.

sentences.zh: 時以正月朔旦有赤氣之異，詣火星觀以禳之，伯雨上疏言：「嘗聞修德以弭災，未有禳祈以消變。

translations.literal: At the time there was an anomaly of red vapor on the first day of the first month; they went to the Temple of the Fire Star to exorcise it; Boyu submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that cultivating virtue quiets disasters—never that exorcism and prayer dispels anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a red vapor appeared on New Year's Day, and the court went to the Temple of the Fire Star to perform exorcisms. Boyu submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that disasters are quieted by cultivating virtue, not by exorcism and prayer.

sentences.zh: 《洪範》以五事配五行，說者謂視之不明，則有赤眚、赤祥。

translations.literal: The Hong Fan pairs the five affairs with the five phases; commentators say that when vision is not clear, there are red calamities and red omens.
translations.idiomatic: The Hong Fan pairs the five human affairs with the five phases, and commentators hold that when vision is unclear, red calamities and red omens appear.

sentences.zh: 乞攬權綱以信賞罰，專威福以殊功罪，使皇明赫赫，事至必斷，則乖氣異象，轉為休祥矣。

translations.literal: I beg that you gather the reins of power to make rewards and punishments credible, concentrate authority and favor to distinguish merit from crime, so that imperial clarity shines bright and matters are decided at once—then perverse qi and strange omens will turn to blessings.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to gather the reins of power so that rewards and punishments carry weight, to concentrate authority so that merit and crime are clearly distinguished, and to let imperial clarity shine so brightly that every matter is decided at once. Then perverse qi and strange omens will turn into blessings."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「比日內降浸多，或恐矯傳制命。

translations.literal: He also said: "Recently inner edicts have grown numerous; I fear some may forge and transmit imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Recently inner edicts have grown ever more numerous, and I fear some may be forged and circulated as imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 漢之鴻都賣爵，唐之墨敕斜封，此近監也。」

translations.literal: The Hongdu sale of offices in Han, the ink-edict sealed slant in Tang—these are recent warnings.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongdu sale of offices in Han and the slant-sealed ink edicts of Tang are warnings close at hand."

sentences.zh: 王覿除御史中丞，仍兼史官，伯雨謂：「史院宰相監修，今中丞為屬，非所以重風憲，遠嫌疑。

translations.literal: Wang Di was appointed Censor-in-Chief while still holding historian duties; Boyu said: "In the Historiography Institute the chief minister supervises compilation—now the censor-in-chief is subordinate to him; this does not weight the integrity of the censorate or keep one far from suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Di was appointed Censor-in-Chief while still serving as a historian. Boyu said, "In the Historiography Institute the chief minister supervises compilation, yet now the censor-in-chief is made subordinate to him. That neither strengthens the censorate nor keeps one above suspicion."

sentences.zh: 」已而覿除翰林，伯雨復論曰：「學士爵秩位序，皆在中丞上。

translations.literal: Soon Di was appointed Hanlin Academician; Boyu argued again: "Academicians in rank and precedence all stand above the censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Di was appointed Hanlin Academician, and Boyu argued again, "Academicians in rank and precedence all stand above the censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 今覿為之，是諫官論事，非特朝廷不行，適足以為人遷官爾。」

translations.literal: Now Di holds that post—this means remonstrance officials debate affairs and the court not only does not follow, but enough to serve as someone's promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Now Di holds that very post. So when remonstrance officials speak out, the court not only ignores them—it effectively hands the criticized man his next promotion."

sentences.zh: 伯雨居諫省半歲，所上一百八疏，大臣畏其多言，俾權給事中，密諭以少默即為真。

translations.literal: Boyu served in the remonstrance bureau half a year, submitting 108 memorials; chief ministers feared his prolixity, made him acting Supervising Secretary, secretly hinting that if he spoke less he would get the real post.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu served in the remonstrance bureau for half a year and submitted one hundred eight memorials. The chief ministers, fearing his ceaseless speech, made him acting Supervising Secretary and secretly hinted that if he spoke less he would receive the permanent appointment.

sentences.zh: 伯雨不聽，抗論愈力，且將劾曾布。

translations.literal: Boyu would not listen, argued with greater force, and was about to impeach Zeng Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu would not listen. He argued all the more forcefully and was about to impeach Zeng Bu.

sentences.zh: 布覺之，徙為度支員外郎，尋知虢州。

translations.literal: Bu noticed, transferred him to Vice Director of Revenue, soon prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bu noticed and had him transferred to Vice Director of Revenue, and soon afterward sent him out as prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇寧黨事作，削籍編管通州。

translations.literal: When the Chongning faction ban arose, his name was stricken from the rolls and he was registered for supervision in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongning faction ban arose, his name was stricken from the rolls and he was placed under registered supervision in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為蔡卞所陷，與陳瓘、龔夬、張庭堅等十三人皆南遷，獨伯雨徙昌化。

translations.literal: Framed by Cai Bian, with Chen Guan, Gong Fu, Zhang Tingjian and thirteen others all sent south, alone Boyu was moved to Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: Framed by Cai Bian, he was exiled together with Chen Guan, Gong Fu, Zhang Tingjian, and thirteen others, all sent south—Boyu alone was transferred to Changhua.

sentences.zh: 姦人猶未甘心，用匿名書復逮其仲子申先赴獄，妻適死於淮，報訃俱至。

translations.literal: Villains were still not satisfied; using an anonymous letter they again seized his second son Shenxian and sent him to prison; his wife happened to die at Huai—both messages of death arrived together.
translations.idiomatic: The villains were still not satisfied. Using an anonymous letter they again seized his second son Shenxian and sent him to prison. His wife happened to die on the Huai River, and both messages of death arrived together.

sentences.zh: 伯雨處之如平常，曰：「死者已矣，生者有負於朝廷，亦當從此訣。

translations.literal: Boyu took it as usual, saying: "The dead are gone; the living have failed the court— I should also take leave here.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu received the news as calmly as on any other day and said, "The dead are gone. The living have failed the court, and I too should take my leave here.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，天豈殺無辜耶！

translations.literal: If that is not so, would Heaven kill the innocent!
translations.idiomatic: If that is not so, would Heaven kill the innocent?"

sentences.zh: 」申先在獄，鍛煉無所傅致，乃得釋，居海上三年而歸。

translations.literal: Shenxian in prison—though tortured, they could attach no charge, and he was released; after three years by the sea he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxian was tortured in prison, but no charge could be made to stick, and he was released. After three years by the sea he returned home.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: Early in Xuanhe he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xuanhe era he died, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 長子象先，登世科，又中詞學兼茂舉，有司啟封，見為黨人子，不奏名，調秦州戶曹掾。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xiangxian passed the hereditary degree, also passed the Combined Eloquence and Learning examination; when the officials opened the sealed list and saw he was a faction member's son, they did not publish his name; he was assigned as revenue section clerk in Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xiangxian passed the hereditary examination and also passed the Combined Eloquence and Learning examination, but when the officials opened the sealed list and saw that he was a faction member's son, they withheld his name. He was assigned as revenue section clerk in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 聞父謫，棄官歸養。

translations.literal: Hearing of his father's banishment, he abandoned office to return and support him.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned of his father's banishment, he resigned his post and returned home to support him.

sentences.zh: 王安中辟燕山宣撫幕，勉應之，道引疾還，終身不復仕。

translations.literal: Wang Anzhong recruited him to the Yan Mountain pacification commission staff; reluctantly he agreed, but on the road cited illness and returned, never holding office again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anzhong recruited him to the Yan Mountain Pacification Commission, and he reluctantly agreed. On the road, however, he pleaded illness and turned back, and never held office again.

sentences.zh: 申先以布衣特起至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Shenxian rose from commoner by special appointment to Secretariat Drafting Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxian rose from commoner by special appointment all the way to Secretariat Drafting Grandee.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，高宗詔贈伯雨直龍圖閣，又加諫議大夫，采其諫章，追貶章惇、蔡卞、邢恕、黃履，明著誣宣仁事以告天下。

translations.literal: Early in Shaoxing, Gaozong edict posthumously enfeoffed Boyu as Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, also adding Remonstrance Grandee, adopting his remonstrance memorials to posthumously demote Zhang Dun, Cai Bian, Xing Shu, Huang Lü, clearly publishing the slander of Empress Xuanren to inform the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shaoxing era, Gaozong issued an edict posthumously granting Boyu the title Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and adding Remonstrance Grandee. Drawing on his remonstrance memorials, the court posthumously demoted Zhang Dun, Cai Bian, Xing Shu, and Huang Lü, and clearly published the slander against Empress Xuanren for all the realm to see.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，賜諡「忠敏」。

translations.literal: In the Chunxi era he was granted the posthumous title Loyal and Perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunxi era he was granted the posthumous title Loyal and Perceptive.

sentences.zh: 論曰：劉安世復文彥博之言，時年尚少，然其言即元祐之初政，而司馬光之用心也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Liu Anshi repeated Wen Yanbo's words; though still young, his speech was exactly the early Yuanyou administration—and Sima Guang's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Liu Anshi repeated Wen Yanbo's words. Though still young, what he said was exactly the early policy of the Yuanyou era—and exactly what Sima Guang had intended.

sentences.zh: 鄒浩諫立劉后，反復曲折，極人所難言。

translations.literal: Zou Hao remonstrated against enthroning Empress Liu—turning and bending, saying what men find hardest to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Hao remonstrated against enthroning Empress Liu, turning and bending through every difficulty, saying what most men cannot bring themselves to say.

sentences.zh: 二人除言官，俱入白其母，母俱勉以盡忠報國，無分毫顧慮後患意。

translations.literal: When the two were appointed remonstrance officials, both went in to tell their mothers; both mothers urged them to devote loyalty to the state, without a particle of thought for later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When the two were appointed remonstrance officials, each went in to tell his mother, and each mother urged him to devote himself wholly to the state, without a thought for the consequences.

sentences.zh: 鳴呼，賢哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how worthy they were!

sentences.zh: 陳瓘、任伯雨抗跡疏遠，立朝寡援，而力發章惇、曾布、蔡京、蔡卞群姦之罪，無少畏忌，古所謂剛正不撓者歟！

translations.literal: Chen Guan and Ren Boyu stood apart in righteous isolation, had few allies at court, yet vigorously exposed the crimes of Zhang Dun, Zeng Bu, Cai Jing, Cai Bian and the pack of villains—without the least fear—are they not what antiquity called steadfast and incorruptible!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan and Ren Boyu stood apart in righteous isolation and had few allies at court, yet they vigorously exposed the crimes of Zhang Dun, Zeng Bu, Cai Jing, Cai Bian, and their whole pack of villains without the least fear. Are they not what antiquity called steadfast and incorruptible?
